concepts/agent-sandboxing.md.name: Agent sandboxing
concepts/agent-sandboxing.md.answer: Agent sandboxing is the architecture that isolates an AI agent's code execution from the infrastructure and secrets it must never reach. Browser Use moved from isolating only the tool to isolating the whole agent, which holds no secrets and reaches the outside only through a control plane, a choice that matters for anyone running code-executing scraping agents at scale.

concepts/ai-web-api-fingerprinting.md.name: AI Web API Fingerprinting
concepts/ai-web-api-fingerprinting.md.answer: AI Web API fingerprinting uses the availability and inference speed of Chrome's on-device AI APIs, such as Summarizer and LanguageModel, as a probe of real hardware capability. For scrapers, it exposes spoofed profiles: a claimed high-end machine that fails availability or timing checks looks inconsistent, though DataDome calls the technique experimental as of April 2026.

concepts/anti-detect-browsers.md.name: Anti-detect browsers
concepts/anti-detect-browsers.md.answer: Anti-detect browsers are Chromium or Firefox forks that attach a fingerprint from a real device database to the automation session. In the tests, GoLogin needed a Mac profile with real WebGL values to pass Harrods but stayed inconsistent, Kameleo passed with residential proxies, and Camoufox now matches them for Cloudflare.

concepts/api-scraping.md.name: API scraping
concepts/api-scraping.md.answer: API scraping means replicating the internal HTTP requests a site's browser or app makes, so you get structured JSON instead of parsing HTML. Check it first on any target: Algolia endpoints on EndClothing.com and Michelin Guide worked without anti-bot bypass, while Castle.io tokens and Booking.com's encrypted parameters could not be replicated.

concepts/bot-detection.md.title: Bot detection: signal layers and what scrapers leak
concepts/bot-detection.md.description: How bot detection works across network, protocol, browser, fingerprint and behavioral layers, with TLS and CDP signals, and why detection exceeds blocking.
concepts/bot-detection.md.name: Bot detection
concepts/bot-detection.md.answer: Bot detection is the discipline of identifying automated traffic and separating it from human visitors, using network, protocol, browser, fingerprint, and behavioral signals. For scrapers, vendors often detect more than they block, so passing can reflect lenient thresholds, and mismatched fingerprints across a fleet can get all of it blocked.

concepts/browser-fingerprinting.md.title: Browser fingerprinting: signals, red flags, test tools
concepts/browser-fingerprinting.md.description: Canvas, WebGL, AudioContext, font and DOM signals, red flags like SwiftShader, extension probing, and the CreepJS and BrowserScan test tools.
concepts/browser-fingerprinting.md.name: Browser fingerprinting
concepts/browser-fingerprinting.md.answer: Browser fingerprinting is a stateless, cookieless way to identify browsers by hashing the outputs of browser APIs such as canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, and DOM properties. For scrapers, SwiftShader renderers, zero media devices, and mismatched signals (a Windows Chrome User-Agent with a Linux GPU string) are the flags that expose automation.

concepts/browser-privacy-fingerprinting-.title: Browser privacy fingerprinting defenses: Safari, Brave
concepts/browser-privacy-fingerprinting-.description: How Safari protections, Firefox resistFingerprinting and Brave farbling lower fingerprint entropy, and what it means for scrapers and anti-detect tools.
concepts/browser-privacy-fingerprinting-.name: Browser privacy fingerprinting defenses
concepts/browser-privacy-fingerprinting-.answer: Browser privacy fingerprinting defenses are anti-fingerprinting protections in Safari, Firefox, and Brave that partition storage and add noise to or remove APIs used for device identification, making classic fingerprints low-entropy. For scrapers, blending in on those surfaces gets easier, but spoofing tools must match each browser's fixed or randomized values, and behavioral and server-side signals remain the resilient detection vectors.

concepts/canvas-fingerprinting.md.title: Canvas fingerprinting: how it works and how defenses fail
concepts/canvas-fingerprinting.md.description: Canvas fingerprinting explained: pixel hashing via toDataURL and getImageData, noise defenses, the Pixel-Recovery attack, Brave Farbling and Camoufox.
concepts/canvas-fingerprinting.md.name: Canvas fingerprinting
concepts/canvas-fingerprinting.md.answer: Canvas fingerprinting is a stateless tracking technique that draws graphics off-screen and hashes the pixels, which differ by GPU, driver, and font rasterizer. For scrapers, the key point is that most randomized-noise defenses were reversed by the 2025 Pixel-Recovery attack, while Brave's Farbling resisted because its noise depends on canvas content.

concepts/cdp-detection.md.title: CDP detection: how Runtime.enable exposes automation
concepts/cdp-detection.md.description: How anti-bots spot Chrome DevTools Protocol control through Runtime.enable, and the fixes: Patchright, Undetected Playwright, Nodriver and Camoufox.
concepts/cdp-detection.md.name: CDP detection
concepts/cdp-detection.md.answer: CDP detection is an anti-bot technique that spots browser automation by observing Chrome DevTools Protocol activity such as Runtime.enable, regardless of JavaScript-level signals. JS stealth patches do not hide it, so scrapers need Patchright, Undetected Playwright, Nodriver, or Camoufox, which controls Firefox through Juggler instead of CDP.

concepts/certificate-pinning.md.description: How mobile apps pin TLS certificates to block proxies like Fiddler and Charles, Android hooks, Frida bypass setup, HTTP Toolkit, iOS and limits.
concepts/certificate-pinning.md.name: Certificate pinning
concepts/certificate-pinning.md.answer: Certificate pinning is a mobile app security mechanism that rejects any TLS certificate not matching an expected certificate or public key, so proxies like Fiddler, Charles, and HTTP Toolkit cannot read traffic even with their CA installed. Scrapers usually bypass it with Frida on a rooted Android device, though third-party services with independent pins, such as Google's, can still block interception.

concepts/cookie-session-reuse.md.description: How clearance cookies from one browser session are reused in an HTTP client. Covers cookie lifetimes by vendor, HTTPX cookie jars and DataDome tests.
concepts/cookie-session-reuse.md.name: Cookie and Session Reuse
concepts/cookie-session-reuse.md.answer: Cookie and session reuse means clearing an anti-bot challenge once in a browser, then exporting the clearance cookies to a browserless HTTP client for many later requests. It pays off when cookies last long, but DataDome worked on Leboncoin, failed on Allegro, and needed another approach on Idealista.

concepts/homepage-first-navigation.md.answer: Homepage-first navigation means loading a site's homepage or entry-point URL before any deep page, so cookies, fingerprint checks, and challenges happen in a real user's order. It cleared initial challenges on several Cloudflare, PerimeterX, and DataDome targets where direct URL access failed, including Antonioli, with no other setup changes.

concepts/http-performance.md.description: Ways to cut scraping time and bandwidth: async requests, ETag conditional requests, HTTP/3 with curl_cffi, connection pre-warming and server co-location.
concepts/http-performance.md.name: HTTP performance in scraping
concepts/http-performance.md.answer: HTTP performance in scraping is the set of techniques that cut execution time, bandwidth, and infrastructure needs without changing the extracted data, mainly concurrency, protocol choice, caching, and retries. In the reported tests, async fetching ran 6x faster on 10 pages, ETag conditional requests cut Shopify bandwidth to 0 bytes on a second pass, and server location mattered most.

concepts/hybrid-scraping.md.name: Hybrid scraping
concepts/hybrid-scraping.md.answer: Hybrid scraping uses a full browser only to clear anti-bot checks and log in, then passes the session cookies to a lightweight HTTP client for data requests. The page reports a 27x speedup over browser-only on one target, and on Net-a-Porter (Akamai) Camoufox with curl_cffi worked while httpx timed out silently.

concepts/inventory-tracking.md.title: Inventory tracking: scraping retail stock levels
concepts/inventory-tracking.md.description: Where sites expose stock data (list page, product page, click-and-collect), how to read the numbers, and tests on Lululemon, Stone Island and IKEA.
concepts/inventory-tracking.md.name: Inventory tracking
concepts/inventory-tracking.md.answer: Inventory tracking is the practice of scraping stock levels that retail sites expose for availability and pickup features, then collecting them repeatedly as a time series. In the tests, Farfetch, IKEA, Stone Island and Lululemon exposed usable data, while large Lowe's and On quantities pointed to warehouse stock.

concepts/javascript-proxy-tracing.md.title: JavaScript Proxy tracing: log properties a script reads
concepts/javascript-proxy-tracing.md.description: How a Proxy over the global object logs property reads and calls of an anti-bot script, as used on SearchGuard with a tapped/untapped control.
concepts/javascript-proxy-tracing.md.name: JavaScript Proxy tracing
concepts/javascript-proxy-tracing.md.answer: JavaScript Proxy tracing is a reverse-engineering technique that runs an anti-bot script against a Proxy standing in for the global object, logging every property read, in check and call without reversing the script. On Google SearchGuard it logged 84 accesses once nested objects were wrapped, but each trace needs a tapped versus untapped token comparison to prove the script did not notice.

concepts/llm-scraping.md.title: LLM scraping: extraction, code generation and limits
concepts/llm-scraping.md.description: Four LLM scraping patterns (schema extraction, vision, code generation, self-healing) with ScrapeGraphAI tests on Net-A-Porter, TripAdvisor and GitHub.
concepts/llm-scraping.md.name: LLM scraping
concepts/llm-scraping.md.answer: LLM scraping uses a large language model to extract structured data from web pages, or to write the scraper code that does it. In the tests reported, it worked best for generating scrapers on well-known sites and for multi-site projects, but hallucinated prices on Net-A-Porter, cost $400 per 10,000 URLs, and cannot reach data absent from the HTML.

concepts/location-data-scraping.md.title: Location data scraping: world grid and bounding box
concepts/location-data-scraping.md.description: Radius and bounding box APIs, the world grid method, Playwright geolocation injection, and tests on Airbnb, Lowe's, Glovo and Alexander McQueen.
concepts/location-data-scraping.md.name: Location data scraping
concepts/location-data-scraping.md.answer: Location data scraping extracts spatially indexed data, such as store locators, listings, and delivery zones, from APIs that take coordinates, a radius, or a bounding box. Full coverage usually needs a world grid of squares, as tested on Airbnb, Glovo, and Lowe's, where stock numbers may reflect regional warehouses.

concepts/ml-bot-detection.md.title: ML-based bot detection: signals and what evades it
concepts/ml-bot-detection.md.description: How ML models flag bots from request, behavioral and fingerprint signals, with TWSC tests of Playwright, undetected-chromedriver and isHumanCadence.
concepts/ml-bot-detection.md.name: ML-based bot detection
concepts/ml-bot-detection.md.answer: ML-based bot detection uses machine learning models to classify web traffic as human or automated, learning from behavioral patterns instead of static rules. All major anti-bot vendors use it, so a bypass must fool the model; in the February 2023 matrix, Playwright with Chrome performed worst and Playwright with Firefox did significantly better.

concepts/mobile-app-scraping.md.title: Mobile app scraping: intercepting app APIs and pinning
concepts/mobile-app-scraping.md.description: How to scrape apps by intercepting their API traffic with a MITM proxy, bypass certificate pinning with Frida, and replicate calls. Tested on Tractor Supply.
concepts/mobile-app-scraping.md.name: Mobile app scraping
concepts/mobile-app-scraping.md.answer: Mobile app scraping means intercepting an app's network traffic with a man-in-the-middle proxy and replicating its API calls in a scraper. App APIs often have lighter anti-bot protection than websites, and one anti-bot that blocked a site was bypassed through the app, but certificate pinning usually needs Frida.

concepts/mobile-proxy-farming.md.title: Mobile proxy farming: USB modems, CGNAT IPs and costs
concepts/mobile-proxy-farming.md.description: Build a mobile proxy farm with USB modems, 3proxy and a modem watchdog. Covers the Raspberry Pi build, Airproxy's 2,000 modems, IP rotation and cost per GB.
concepts/mobile-proxy-farming.md.name: Mobile proxy farming
concepts/mobile-proxy-farming.md.answer: Mobile proxy farming is running your own USB modems or SIM hardware to route proxy traffic through real cellular connections, giving CGNAT mobile IPs you control and rotate. Mobile IPs are hard for anti-bot systems to block, so they help on luxury fashion, ticketing, and sneaker sites, and owning the farm pays off at high volume.

concepts/mouse-movement-emulation.md.title: Mouse movement emulation: Bezier, Gaussian, Perlin
concepts/mouse-movement-emulation.md.description: Mouse emulation algorithms (ghost-cursor Bezier, OxyMouse Gaussian and Perlin), tested on DataDome and Cloudflare, plus Akamai's MACT detection.
concepts/mouse-movement-emulation.md.name: Mouse movement emulation
concepts/mouse-movement-emulation.md.answer: Mouse movement emulation generates human-like pointer trajectories during browser automation, using Bezier curves (ghost-cursor), Gaussian noise, or Perlin noise (OxyMouse). In the reported tests it got past DataDome on hermes.com where Playwright's native mouse.move() failed, while Cloudflare does not use mouse events, so it can be skipped there.

concepts/prerender-stealth-request.md.title: Prerender Stealth Request: CSP bypass and real UA leak
concepts/prerender-stealth-request.md.description: How link rel=prerender in Chromium skips CSP, hides from the DevTools Network tab and leaks the real User-Agent, plus the Sec-Purpose: prefetch signature.
concepts/prerender-stealth-request.md.name: Prerender Stealth Request
concepts/prerender-stealth-request.md.answer: Prerender Stealth Request is a Chromium-only technique where a link rel=prerender element fires a GET request that bypasses CSP, skips the DevTools Network tab, and sends the browser's real User-Agent even under a DevTools UA override, exposing spoofed scrapers. It carries no body and no cross-origin cookies, and defenders can block it via its Sec-Purpose: prefetch signature.

concepts/proxy-fundamentals.md.title: Proxy fundamentals: proxy types, IP reputation, costs
concepts/proxy-fundamentals.md.description: Datacenter, ISP, residential and mobile proxies compared, with CGNAT, ASN and subnet blocking, X-Forwarded-For, per-GB costs, and pool sizing.
concepts/proxy-fundamentals.md.name: Proxy fundamentals
concepts/proxy-fundamentals.md.answer: Proxy fundamentals covers how datacenter, ISP, residential, and mobile proxies route requests through another IP, and why IP reputation, ASN, and network type often matter more than browser signals. Mobile IPs are hard to block because of CGNAT, and one tested provider sold datacenter IPs as residential.

concepts/scraping-economics.md.title: Scraping economics: costs, business models, margins
concepts/scraping-economics.md.description: Scraping cost categories (setup, proxies, maintenance), why web data firms scale poorly, and business models from freelance work to data marketplaces.
concepts/scraping-economics.md.name: Scraping economics
concepts/scraping-economics.md.answer: Scraping economics covers the setup, running, and maintenance costs of scraping operations, the business models for selling scraped data, and the market dynamics of the web data industry. Proxies are the dominant variable cost, each new customer brought about 20% more websites at Re Analytics, and selling infrastructure to scrapers is the most profitable position.

concepts/scraping-infrastructure.md.title: Scraping infrastructure: compute, scheduling, proxies
concepts/scraping-infrastructure.md.description: Compute options (Lambda, Fargate, VMs, bare metal), scheduling with cron, Scrapyd, GitHub Actions and Airflow, Scrapeops monitoring, Scrapoxy proxies.
concepts/scraping-infrastructure.md.name: Scraping infrastructure
concepts/scraping-infrastructure.md.answer: Scraping infrastructure is the compute, storage, scheduling, monitoring, and proxy systems that run scrapers reliably at scale, and it sets cost, IP rotation, and operational overhead. In the tests, AWS Lambda gave a fresh datacenter IP per call, GitHub Actions ran scheduled Scrapy spiders, and Airflow chained scraping to S3 uploads.

concepts/static-isp-proxies.md.title: Static ISP proxies: sourcing, sale model and detection
concepts/static-isp-proxies.md.description: Static ISP proxies: BYOP and IPXO sourcing, fake ISPs, per-IP sale tiers, and detection through tunnel labels, WHOIS, Ashburn and GRE source ports.
concepts/static-isp-proxies.md.name: Static ISP proxies
concepts/static-isp-proxies.md.answer: Static ISP proxies are datacenter-hosted IPs from real or fake ISP address blocks, assigned to one customer for weeks or months. They avoid datacenter ASN blocklists and respond fast, which suits account management, but threat intelligence can tag fully proxy-only subnets as tunnels and flag IPXO-leased ranges.

concepts/tls-fingerprinting.md.title: TLS fingerprinting: how JA3 and JA4 expose scrapers
concepts/tls-fingerprinting.md.description: How JA3, JA4 and HTTP/2 fingerprints flag Python clients on Akamai and Cloudflare, plus the fixes tested: curl_cffi, JA3Proxy, scrapy-impersonate.
concepts/tls-fingerprinting.md.name: TLS fingerprinting
concepts/tls-fingerprinting.md.answer: TLS fingerprinting identifies an HTTPS client from its ClientHello message, usually as a JA3 or JA4 hash, before any HTTP data is sent. Python's default stack gets flagged on Akamai and Cloudflare targets whatever headers are set, so scrapers need TLS impersonation such as curl_cffi.

concepts/vm-based-javascript-obfuscation.title: VM-based JavaScript obfuscation: how anti-bots hide checks
concepts/vm-based-javascript-obfuscation.description: How anti-bot scripts hide detection in a JavaScript VM with encrypted bytecode, using Google SearchGuard as the example, and what works against it.
concepts/vm-based-javascript-obfuscation.name: VM-based JavaScript obfuscation
concepts/vm-based-javascript-obfuscation.answer: VM-based JavaScript obfuscation ships an interpreter plus an encrypted bytecode program, so the detection checks and token assembly never appear as readable script text. For scrapers, patches tied to one property or function name last one build, as seen with Google SearchGuard, which rebuilt five times in a month. Nothing was tested on this page.

concepts/web-scraping-legal-landscape.md.title: Web scraping legality: CFAA, DMCA, ToS, GDPR, cases
concepts/web-scraping-legal-landscape.md.description: Legal frameworks for scraping: CFAA, DMCA Section 1201, ToS, robots.txt, copyright, GDPR. Cases: hiQ v. LinkedIn, Bright Data, Google v. SerpApi.
concepts/web-scraping-legal-landscape.md.name: Legal web scraping
concepts/web-scraping-legal-landscape.md.answer: Legal web scraping is governed by no single statute, drawing on the CFAA, DMCA Section 1201, copyright, contract terms, and GDPR, and courts are still defining the limits. For scrapers, the CFAA is weak against public pages, while DMCA circumvention claims, as in Google v. SerpApi, are the growing risk.

concepts/web-unblockers.md.title: Web unblockers: managed anti-bot bypass APIs tested
concepts/web-unblockers.md.description: How unblockers differ from proxies and BaaS, plus test results on Cloudflare, DataDome, Kasada and PerimeterX for Zyte, Oxylabs and Smartproxy.
concepts/web-unblockers.md.name: Web unblockers
concepts/web-unblockers.md.answer: Web unblockers are managed APIs that take a target URL and return page content, handling IP rotation, CAPTCHAs, and fingerprinting on the provider's side. In the tests reported, Cloudflare and PerimeterX were passed by most providers, Kasada by Bright Data, Oxylabs, and Smartproxy, and DataDome was the hardest target.

concepts/webdriver-vs-cdp-vs-bidi.md.title: WebDriver vs CDP vs WebDriver BiDi: detection surface
concepts/webdriver-vs-cdp-vs-bidi.md.description: Compares the three browser automation protocols and the detection vectors each exposes: navigator.webdriver, Runtime.enable, Juggler in Camoufox, and BiDi.
concepts/webdriver-vs-cdp-vs-bidi.md.name: WebDriver vs CDP vs WebDriver BiDi
concepts/webdriver-vs-cdp-vs-bidi.md.answer: WebDriver vs CDP vs WebDriver BiDi compares three browser automation protocols that differ in transport, browser support, and detection surface. WebDriver exposes navigator.webdriver, CDP exposes the Runtime.enable signal, and BiDi's surface is not yet characterized, while Camoufox avoids CDP by using the Juggler protocol.

concepts/webrtc-ip-leak.md.title: WebRTC IP leak: real IP behind a proxy and fixes
concepts/webrtc-ip-leak.md.description: How WebRTC ICE and STUN candidates expose the real IP behind an HTTP proxy. Covers Firefox defenses and the Camoufox 146 and fork test results.
concepts/webrtc-ip-leak.md.name: WebRTC IP leak
concepts/webrtc-ip-leak.md.answer: WebRTC IP leak is when a page reads a client's real LAN or WAN IP through WebRTC ICE candidates while HTTP traffic goes through a proxy, creating a detectable mismatch. In the 2026-06 tests, stock Camoufox 146 behind an HTTP proxy leaked the real WAN IP, while the JWriter20 fork gathered zero candidates.

concepts/websocket-bot-detection.md.title: WebSocket bot detection: signals and countermeasures
concepts/websocket-bot-detection.md.description: How servers detect bots over WebSocket: handshake fingerprinting, honeypot events, connection lifecycle, ping jitter, TLS and countermeasures.
concepts/websocket-bot-detection.md.name: WebSocket bot detection
concepts/websocket-bot-detection.md.answer: WebSocket bot detection is a set of anti-bot techniques that use the persistent, stateful WebSocket connection to spot automated clients, including handshake checks, connection lifecycle analysis, honeypot events, and repeated fingerprinting. For scrapers, send a browser-matching handshake with an Origin header, add random delays, rotate proxies, and look for HTTP API alternatives. The page's coverage is conceptual, with no bypass tests.

concepts/websocket-scraping.md.title: WebSocket scraping: connect to real-time feeds directly
concepts/websocket-scraping.md.description: How to find a WebSocket endpoint in DevTools and replay its subscription in Python. Covers Bitstamp JSON, Sofascore NATS keepalive and Polymarket feeds.
concepts/websocket-scraping.md.name: WebSocket scraping
concepts/websocket-scraping.md.answer: WebSocket scraping means connecting directly to a site's WebSocket endpoint, subscribing to the browser's channels, and reading the pushed real-time stream. In the tests reported, Bitstamp's JSON feed worked with no authentication, while Sofascore's NATS protocol dropped the connection after a few minutes without PING/PONG keepalive.

entities/3rd-party-proxy.md.title: 3rd Party Proxy: residential IPs for TraceAIO browser runs
entities/3rd-party-proxy.md.description: 3rd Party Proxy is the TraceAIO browser runtime. It routes prompts through Apify residential proxies with a new IP per request for ChatGPT and Perplexity.
entities/3rd-party-proxy.md.name: 3rd Party Proxy
entities/3rd-party-proxy.md.answer: 3rd Party Proxy is the browser runtime recommended for the TraceAIO project, routing requests through residential proxies provided via Apify. Each request gets a different IP address, which is meant to avoid anti-bot issues for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Mode sessions. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/4chan-captcha-solver.md.title: 4chan CAPTCHA solver: ML model for text and slider
entities/4chan-captcha-solver.md.description: Project training a browser-run ML model on 4chan's alphanumeric and slider CAPTCHAs, with data scraping, throttling, and Cloudflare Turnstile cookie limits.
entities/4chan-captcha-solver.md.name: 4chan CAPTCHA Solver
entities/4chan-captcha-solver.md.answer: The 4chan CAPTCHA Solver is a project that trains a machine learning model to solve 4chan's alphanumeric and slider CAPTCHAs, aiming for over 80% accuracy in the browser. For scrapers, collecting training data requires valid cookies to pass Cloudflare Turnstile, and heavy request volume throttles access and degrades data quality. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/aegis.md.title: Aegis: open-source Go WAF and reverse proxy vs bots
entities/aegis.md.description: Aegis is an open-source Go WAF and reverse proxy that blocks bots with OWASP CRS rules, rate limiting, IP access control and an admin console. Not yet tested.
entities/aegis.md.name: Aegis
entities/aegis.md.answer: Aegis is an open-source Web Application Firewall and reverse proxy written in Go that inspects HTTP and HTTPS traffic at the network edge. It applies OWASP Core Rule Set defense, rate limiting, IP access control, and protocol enforcement against malicious bots and traffic surges, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ag2b.md.title: AG2B: client-side agent runtime in the browser
entities/ag2b.md.description: AG2B (Agent to Browser) runs an LLM agent inside the user's browser with DOM access. Covers The Loop, tool execution and the thin LLM proxy server option.
entities/ag2b.md.name: AG2B
entities/ag2b.md.answer: AG2B (Agent to Browser) is a client-side agentic runtime that runs an agent inside the user's browser, where it can work with the DOM. Its Agent runs a loop in which the LLM picks a Tool and executes it in the browser. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/agent-vault-proxy.md.title: agent-vault-proxy: just-in-time API keys for AI agents
entities/agent-vault-proxy.md.description: Loopback HTTPS proxy that swaps placeholders for real secrets from Bitwarden Secrets Manager, with host and path bindings and audit logging.
entities/agent-vault-proxy.md.name: agent-vault-proxy
entities/agent-vault-proxy.md.answer: agent-vault-proxy is a loopback HTTPS proxy that gives AI agents and other processes a placeholder string, then swaps in the real API key from Bitwarden Secrets Manager on the outbound request. It fails closed when no binding matches the destination, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/agent-web-crawlers.md.title: Agent web crawlers: 60 named bots seen on one endpoint
entities/agent-web-crawlers.md.description: Census of 60 named agent crawlers hitting one endpoint: liveness checks, directory indexing, security research and price-quote scraping.
entities/agent-web-crawlers.md.name: Agent web crawlers
entities/agent-web-crawlers.md.answer: Agent web crawlers are named bots and agents that probe, grade, index, and scrape endpoints. A census found 60 distinct ones hitting a single endpoint, and many only check liveness or read price quotes without paying or invoking tools; TWSC has not tested them yet.

entities/ai-agent-reader-page.md.title: AI Agent Reader Page: human vs agent content
entities/ai-agent-reader-page.md.description: Specimen page showing a developer-tools landing page to humans and a separate passage for agents in a template data-agent-readable tag. Not yet tested.
entities/ai-agent-reader-page.md.name: AI Agent Reader Page
entities/ai-agent-reader-page.md.answer: AI Agent Reader Page is a specimen page that shows one version of a developer-tools landing page to humans and a separate passage to software agents. The agent text sits in a `<template data-agent-readable>` tag in the server HTML, unrendered for people. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ai-generated-content-detection..title: AI-generated content detection: spotting LLM social bots
entities/ai-generated-content-detection..description: How an adversarial method builds a multilingual, cross-platform dataset of paired human and AI messages to train detectors of LLM-written social bot text.
entities/ai-generated-content-detection..name: AI-generated content detection
entities/ai-generated-content-detection..answer: AI-generated content detection is research on identifying text that large language models produce for social bot operations. Its detectors are trained on an adversarial, multilingual, cross-platform dataset of paired human and AI messages and outperform existing content-based bot detection on real-world, out-of-distribution data. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ai-page-audit-tool.md.title: AI Page Audit Tool: checks if LLMs can read and cite a page
entities/ai-page-audit-tool.md.description: Free tool that scores a public page on Reach, Read and Trust for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI. Covers robots.txt, noindex, JSON-LD and limits.
entities/ai-page-audit-tool.md.name: AI Page Audit Tool
entities/ai-page-audit-tool.md.answer: AI Page Audit Tool is a free utility that checks whether a public webpage can be read and quoted by large language models, scoring it on Reach, Read, and Trust. It flags blockers like robots.txt rules, noindex tags, and content that needs JavaScript. TWSC has not tested it, and it cannot audit pages behind a login.

entities/aiohttp.md.title: AIOHTTP: async Python HTTP client for parallel scraping
entities/aiohttp.md.description: aiohttp is an asyncio HTTP client and server for Python, used to build bots and scrapers that send requests in parallel. Lists its user agent string.
entities/aiohttp.md.name: AIOHTTP
entities/aiohttp.md.answer: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client and server library for Python's asyncio, identifiable by a default user agent like Python/3.x aiohttp/3.x.x. Scrapers and bots use it to send many requests in parallel, though TWSC has not yet tested it against any protected sites.

entities/akamai-v3-sensor-data.md.title: Akamai v3 sensor data: two-step payload encryption
entities/akamai-v3-sensor-data.md.description: How Akamai v3 sensor data is encrypted: a PRNG shuffle seeded by a script hash, then a substitution seeded by the bm_sz cookie hash. Not yet tested.
entities/akamai-v3-sensor-data.md.name: Akamai v3 sensor data
entities/akamai-v3-sensor-data.md.answer: Akamai v3 sensor data is the payload Akamai's bot protection collects to detect bots, protected by a two-step encryption. A PRNG seeded with a JavaScript file hash shuffles the data, then one seeded with a bm_sz cookie hash substitutes characters. Both dependencies complicate bypassing it, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/akamai.md.title: Akamai Bot Manager: detection methods and bypasses
entities/akamai.md.description: How Akamai Bot Manager detects bots through TLS, _abck cookies, IP reputation and mouse data, and what worked on Gucci, Zalando, H&M and Nike.
entities/akamai.md.name: Akamai Bot Manager
entities/akamai.md.answer: Akamai Bot Manager is Akamai's anti-bot product, combining TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprinting, a behavioral JavaScript sensor, and cloud ML scoring. For public data, browser-accurate TLS fingerprints via curl_cffi bypassed it in most tests, including 100% of 1,000 Nike.com URLs, while AWS IPs were blocked fastest.

entities/algolia.md.title: Algolia: scraping product search API endpoints
entities/algolia.md.description: How to find and query Algolia search endpoints: the x-algolia-* parameters, POST body formats, pagination, and tests on EndClothing and Michelin Guide.
entities/algolia.md.name: Algolia
entities/algolia.md.answer: Algolia is a search-as-a-service platform that many e-commerce sites use to query their product catalogs, with search-only keys exposed in the page's JavaScript. Scraping its endpoints is often easier than parsing HTML: on EndClothing, which was protected by Akamai, the Algolia endpoint had no anti-bot protection and returned the full catalog.

entities/antigravity-proxy.md.title: antigravity-proxy: local Node.js TLS-terminating proxy
entities/antigravity-proxy.md.description: Local Node.js proxy that terminates TLS on ports 4000/443 with a self-signed wildcard certificate, strips inline system prompts and rebuilds mock headers.
entities/antigravity-proxy.md.name: antigravity-proxy
entities/antigravity-proxy.md.answer: antigravity-proxy is a local Node.js proxy that terminates TLS on ports 4000/443 with a self-signed wildcard certificate to intercept traffic bound for Google's generative language servers for the WhatsApp Coding framework. It strips repeated system prompts and metadata and rebuilds mock headers, but TWSC has not tested it.

entities/anvil.md.title: Anvil: GitHub API proxy for Forgejo and Codeberg
entities/anvil.md.description: Anvil makes a Forgejo instance look like GitHub for gh, Renovate and CI status tools. Covers Shotgun, mappings.toml, HTTPS needs and 501 unsupported features.
entities/anvil.md.name: Anvil
entities/anvil.md.answer: Anvil is a proxy that lets GitHub-compatible tools such as `gh repo list`, Renovate, and CI status reporting talk to a Forgejo instance as if it were GitHub, using Shotgun and a `mappings.toml` file. It has not been tested by TWSC, needs an HTTPS reverse proxy in front for `gh`, and returns 501 for GraphQL, Packages, and Dependabot.

entities/anycrawl.md.title: AnyCrawl: open-source scraping API for LLM pipelines
entities/anycrawl.md.description: AnyCrawl scrape, search and crawl endpoints, Cheerio, Playwright and Puppeteer engines, JSON schema extraction, MCP server, and its anti-bot limits.
entities/anycrawl.md.name: AnyCrawl
entities/anycrawl.md.answer: AnyCrawl is an MIT-licensed, open-source scraping API for LLM pipelines that returns schema-based JSON through REST endpoints and an MCP server. In January 2026 testing it worked for JSON extraction and self-hosting, but it has no custom headers, TLS fingerprinting, or CAPTCHA solving, so it fails on targets protected by Cloudflare or DataDome.

entities/apiaxess.md.title: apiaxess: capture mobile and web APIs for scraping
entities/apiaxess.md.description: Open-source tool that captures mobile and web API traffic through a proxy and Android emulator, with request replay, Intruder attacks and OpenAPI export.
entities/apiaxess.md.name: apiaxess
entities/apiaxess.md.answer: apiaxess is an open-source tool that captures, analyzes, and interacts with APIs from mobile and web apps, using a proxied browser and an Android emulator that trusts the certificate. It exports to OpenAPI 3.1, Postman, HAR, and Python, and warns on unbypassable certificate pinning. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/apify.md.title: Apify: pre-built actors and web-to-LLM scrapers
entities/apify.md.description: Apify's pre-built actors and turnkey web-to-LLM scrapers, used for LLM fine-tuning, RAG pipelines and e-commerce monitoring. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/apify.md.name: Apify
entities/apify.md.answer: Apify is a scraping provider that offers pre-built actors and turnkey web-to-LLM scrapers, and a benchmark source names it the best provider for LLMs and Markdown generation. Practitioners use it for LLM fine-tuning, RAG pipelines, and cross-border e-commerce monitoring, though TWSC has not yet tested it.

entities/atproxy.md.title: atproxy: transparent Android app TCP proxy in Rust
entities/atproxy.md.description: atproxy is a Rust tool that uses iptables NAT REDIRECT to send one Android app's TCP traffic, by UID, to an upstream HTTP proxy such as Burp Suite.
entities/atproxy.md.name: atproxy
entities/atproxy.md.answer: atproxy is a Rust program that transparently proxies TCP traffic from a single Android app through an upstream HTTP proxy such as Burp Suite. It uses iptables NAT REDIRECT keyed to the app's UID, so the app needs no proxy settings. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/aws-waf.md.title: AWS WAF: aws-waf-token challenge and how to bypass it
entities/aws-waf.md.description: How AWS WAF issues its JavaScript challenge and aws-waf-token cookie, how to spot it, and the Playwright plus Scrapy cookie approach tested on Traveloka.
entities/aws-waf.md.name: AWS WAF
entities/aws-waf.md.answer: AWS WAF is Amazon Web Services' general-purpose web application firewall, with bot detection that issues a JavaScript challenge and an `aws-waf-token` cookie. On Traveloka.com, plain Scrapy failed, but a Playwright session generated a token that Scrapy API calls reused for four days.

entities/beautiful-code-screenshots-code.title: CodeShot: code screenshot, scrape and preview API
entities/beautiful-code-screenshots-code.description: CodeShot is a REST API with one key for code screenshots, full-page webshots, URL scraping to markdown or text, and Open Graph link previews.
entities/beautiful-code-screenshots-code.name: CodeShot
entities/beautiful-code-screenshots-code.answer: CodeShot is a REST API toolkit for developers and AI agents that generates code screenshots, scrapes URLs into clean markdown or text, captures webpage screenshots, and returns Open Graph link previews with one API key. For scraping, the /v1/scrape and /v1/webshot endpoints are the relevant ones, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/blanktrace.md.title: BlankTrace: Rust MITM proxy that randomizes fingerprints
entities/blanktrace.md.description: BlankTrace is a Rust MITM proxy for Linux and macOS. Covers User-Agent and Accept-Language randomization, cookie stripping, domain blocking and CA setup.
entities/blanktrace.md.name: BlankTrace
entities/blanktrace.md.answer: BlankTrace is a Rust command-line MITM proxy and daemon for Linux and macOS that randomizes User-Agent and Accept-Language headers, strips cookies, and blocks trackers by domain regex. It listens on localhost:8080 and needs a manually installed CA certificate for HTTPS. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/bot-detection-system.md.title: Bot detection system: layered signals and risk scoring
entities/bot-detection-system.md.description: How a bot detection system combines IP reputation, ASN, TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprinting, and browser signals into a risk score that triggers an action.
entities/bot-detection-system.md.name: Bot detection system
entities/bot-detection-system.md.answer: A bot detection system separates real users from automation by combining many weak signals from the network, TLS, browser, and behavior into one risk score. For scrapers, the practical point is that contradictory signals, such as a Chrome User-Agent with a Node TLS fingerprint, raise that score. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/botasaurus.md.title: Botasaurus: Python stealth scraping, local vs server
entities/botasaurus.md.description: Botasaurus decorators (@browser, @request, @task) and test results: it passed Cloudflare, DataDome and Kasada on a laptop but fails on cloud servers.
entities/botasaurus.md.name: Botasaurus
entities/botasaurus.md.answer: Botasaurus is a Python scraping framework that wraps a stealth Chromium browser, a TLS-spoofing HTTP client, and parallel task execution in decorators. In TWSC tests, version 4 passed Cloudflare, DataDome, and Kasada from a laptop, but in datacenter deployments it exposed SwiftShader and no media devices, which anti-bot systems flag.

entities/botdeflector-solver-chrome-exte.title: BotDeflector Solver Chrome Extension: solves BotDeflector
entities/botdeflector-solver-chrome-exte.description: Chrome extension that detects and solves the BotDeflector captcha in Queue-IT waiting rooms via TakionAPI. Covers how it works and the Chrome 137 limitation.
entities/botdeflector-solver-chrome-exte.name: BotDeflector Solver Chrome Extension
entities/botdeflector-solver-chrome-exte.answer: BotDeflector Solver Chrome Extension is a browser extension that detects and solves the BotDeflector captcha, which shows up in Queue-IT waiting rooms and custom implementations. It sends captcha images to TakionAPI and clicks as instructed, but TWSC has not tested it, and branded Chrome since version 137 ignores --load-extension.

entities/botdeflector.md.title: BotDeflector: Queue-IT captcha, PoW and icon challenges
entities/botdeflector.md.description: BotDeflector, captcha used with Queue-IT: its obfuscated proof of work graph challenge, icon captcha, botdeflector.eu fingerprint and known weaknesses.
entities/botdeflector.md.name: BotDeflector
entities/botdeflector.md.answer: BotDeflector is a captcha system from Queue-IT co-founder Martin Pronk, often found on Queue-IT queue pages or `/softblock/` pages. It combines an invisible Proof of Work challenge with an icon captcha, and the source reports no rate limits on icon submissions and a SiteKey not bound to a domain; TWSC has not tested it.

entities/botid.md.title: BotID: how Vercel's invisible CAPTCHA detects bots
entities/botid.md.description: BotID is Vercel's invisible CAPTCHA. The page covers its obfuscated c.js script, the client-side signals and crypto API it uses, and related pages.
entities/botid.md.name: BotID
entities/botid.md.answer: BotID is Vercel's invisible CAPTCHA that blocks sophisticated bots without showing a challenge. It loads an obfuscated JavaScript file, c.js, which collects client-side signals and uses the crypto API to judge whether a visitor is automated; it has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/brave-browser.md.title: Brave Browser: unidentified crawler and paywall bypass
entities/brave-browser.md.description: Brave is a privacy-focused browser that built a 30 billion page index with an unidentified crawler publishers could not block it. Not yet tested.
entities/brave-browser.md.name: Brave Browser
entities/brave-browser.md.answer: Brave Browser is a privacy-focused browser from an 11-year-old company. It built an index of more than 30 billion web pages with an unidentified crawler that publishers could not block, and its paywall bypass feature is part of the dispute. The Web Scraping Wiki has not tested it yet.

entities/bright-data.md.title: Bright Data: residential proxies in smart TV app SDKs
entities/bright-data.md.description: Bright Data residential proxy network, how its proxy SDKs are bundled in smart TV apps, and the countermeasures that limit access to local devices.
entities/bright-data.md.name: Bright Data
entities/bright-data.md.answer: Bright Data is a residential proxy network named in research on proxy SDKs embedded in smart TV apps, where a user's device becomes a residential proxy node rented to paying customers. TWSC has not tested it, and the page notes its countermeasures keep customers from reaching other devices on the host's local network.

entities/browser-fingerprint-scanner.md.title: Browser Fingerprint Scanner: live bot risk score test
entities/browser-fingerprint-scanner.md.description: Live tool that checks WebRTC leaks, headers, GPU, DRM support and automation signals, then returns a fingerprint hash and a 0 to 100 bot risk score.
entities/browser-fingerprint-scanner.md.name: Browser Fingerprint Scanner
entities/browser-fingerprint-scanner.md.answer: Browser Fingerprint Scanner is a live testing tool that inspects browser, device, WebRTC leak, network, header, GPU, DRM, and automation signals, then produces a fingerprint hash and a 0 to 100 bot risk score. It has not yet been tested by TWSC, and spoofed attributes can be flagged when they conflict.

entities/browser-use.md.title: Browser Use: undetectable cloud browser, antibot bypass
entities/browser-use.md.description: Browser Use runs a patched Chromium fork against Cloudflare, DataDome, Kasada and Akamai. Covers fingerprints, CAPTCHA solving and Firecracker cloud.
entities/browser-use.md.name: Browser Use
entities/browser-use.md.answer: Browser Use is a cloud browser automation platform built on a custom Chromium fork with C++ and OS-level patches, aimed at being undetectable by antibot systems such as Cloudflare, DataDome, Kasada, and Akamai. It also offers residential proxies, in-house CAPTCHA solving, and Firecracker microVM sessions priced at $0.02 per browser hour.

entities/browserbase-chrome.md.title: Browserbase Chrome: real-browser QA on PR preview deploys
entities/browserbase-chrome.md.description: Browserbase Chrome runs real-browser QA on every pull request against the preview deploy, with residential proxies, DOM rendering, screenshots and video.
entities/browserbase-chrome.md.name: Browserbase Chrome
entities/browserbase-chrome.md.answer: Browserbase Chrome is a real-browser setup used for QA runs against deployed previews of projects. Each pull request runs against the preview deploy with residential proxies, real DOM rendering, and screenshot and video attachments for review, but TWSC has not tested it against any anti-bot systems yet.

entities/bytecode-traversal.md.title: Bytecode Traversal: static disassembly of VM bytecode
entities/bytecode-traversal.md.description: Bytecode Traversal disassembles VM bytecode into pseudocode without running it, by following jumps recursively. Covers how it works and its bloat limitation.
entities/bytecode-traversal.md.name: Bytecode Traversal
entities/bytecode-traversal.md.answer: Bytecode Traversal is a static method for disassembling virtual machine bytecode by following jumps recursively and producing readable pseudocode without running the code. For scrapers facing VM-based JavaScript obfuscation it only disassembles reachable code, though it can still bloat on impossible branches, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/camoufox-reverse.md.title: camoufox-reverse: Camoufox fork that traces DOM reads
entities/camoufox-reverse.md.description: Camoufox fork with an engine-level PropertyTracer that logs DOM getters a page reads. Covers setup, limits, and a Datadome trace on leboncoin.fr.
entities/camoufox-reverse.md.name: camoufox-reverse
entities/camoufox-reverse.md.answer: camoufox-reverse is a Camoufox fork by WhiteNightShadow that adds an engine-level PropertyTracer, which logs the DOM getters a page reads without being visible to JavaScript. It is a diagnostic tool, not a stealth browser. In TWSC tests on leboncoin.fr it showed Datadome making 584 reads on ad pages versus 140 on the homepage.

entities/camoufox.md.title: Camoufox: patched Firefox for anti-bot bypass
entities/camoufox.md.description: Camoufox is a custom Firefox build with engine-level fingerprint spoofing. Covers Cloudflare, Kasada and Datadome results, Docker/AWS deployment and forks.
entities/camoufox.md.name: Camoufox
entities/camoufox.md.answer: Camoufox is an open-source Firefox build by daijro, patched and recompiled so fingerprint spoofing happens in the engine instead of through JavaScript injection. In the reported tests it was the best open-source performer against Cloudflare (99% on Harrods) and passed Kasada, but Datadome on hermes.com needed workarounds.

entities/canvas-fingerprint-defender.md.title: Canvas fingerprint defender: extension that alters canvas
entities/canvas-fingerprint-defender.md.description: Browser extension that randomizes canvas pixel values to change the canvas fingerprint. Covers how it works, related fingerprinting concepts and Dolphin Anty.
entities/canvas-fingerprint-defender.md.name: Canvas fingerprint defender
entities/canvas-fingerprint-defender.md.answer: Canvas fingerprint defender is a browser extension that randomizes the value of certain canvas pixels, which changes the canvas fingerprint and makes a user harder to identify across sites. It is one countermeasure against canvas fingerprinting, and TWSC has not tested it, so its effect against real anti-bot systems is unreported.

entities/castle.md.title: Castle: how it detects bots on X login and Selenium
entities/castle.md.description: Castle anti-bot on the X (Twitter) login page: per-step encrypted tokens, signals scored server-side, and why Selenium with stealth plugins may be flagged.
entities/castle.md.name: Castle
entities/castle.md.answer: Castle is an anti-bot system used by X (formerly Twitter) that scores a token at each login step to detect automation. Its SDK collects device, environment, and interaction signals, and negative scores lead to login restrictions. TWSC has not tested it, and the source suggests Selenium with stealth plugins may still be flagged.

entities/cfsolve.md.title: cfsolve: Rust Cloudflare Turnstile and challenge solver
entities/cfsolve.md.description: cfsolve is a Rust library and CLI that returns Turnstile tokens or cf_clearance cookies without a headless browser, using recorded browser profiles.
entities/cfsolve.md.name: cfsolve
entities/cfsolve.md.answer: cfsolve is a Rust library and command line tool that solves Cloudflare Turnstile widgets and challenge pages without a full headless browser, returning a Turnstile token or a cf_clearance cookie. It relies on recorded browser profiles, which take manual or AI effort to produce, and supports only Safari and Chrome(ium) types. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/chaser-oxide.md.title: chaser-oxide: Rust stealth browser automation for Chromium
entities/chaser-oxide.md.description: chaser-oxide is a Rust fork of chromiumoxide that patches CDP at the protocol layer. Covers native and spoofed OS profiles (Windows, Linux, macOS) and setup.
entities/chaser-oxide.md.name: chaser-oxide
entities/chaser-oxide.md.answer: Chaser-oxide is a Rust fork of chromiumoxide that patches the Chrome DevTools Protocol at the transport and protocol layer, not through JavaScript wrappers, to reduce the detection footprint of automated Chromium sessions. It auto-detects the host OS, Chrome version, and RAM, and has optional OS spoofing profiles. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/cheerio.md.title: Cheerio: Node.js HTML parsing with jQuery-like selectors
entities/cheerio.md.description: Cheerio is a Node.js library that loads HTML into a jQuery-like structure so selectors can target elements and extract data. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/cheerio.md.name: Cheerio
entities/cheerio.md.answer: Cheerio is a Node.js library that parses HTML and extracts data from web pages. It loads HTML into a structure that accepts jQuery-like selectors to target elements. TWSC has not tested it yet, so the page reports no results on blocking or detection.

entities/childflow.md.title: childflow: Linux network sandbox for one command tree
entities/childflow.md.description: childflow runs one command tree in an isolated Linux network context, forcing proxying without HTTP_PROXY or LD_PRELOAD. Two Linux backends.
entities/childflow.md.name: childflow
entities/childflow.md.answer: childflow is a Linux network sandbox that runs one command and its child processes in an isolated network context, with DNS, host, proxy, policy and capture settings applied only to that tree. It forces proxying at the network path instead of using HTTP_PROXY or LD_PRELOAD, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/chromiumfish.md.title: ChromiumFish: stealth Chromium fork with C++ spoofing
entities/chromiumfish.md.description: ChromiumFish is a Chromium fork that spoofs UA, Client Hints, fonts, audio, screen and WebRTC in C++, with a Playwright harness and a Windows Canvas bridge.
entities/chromiumfish.md.name: ChromiumFish
entities/chromiumfish.md.answer: ChromiumFish is a stealth Chromium fork that hardens fingerprints by spoofing signals such as UA, Client Hints, fonts, audio, screen, and WebRTC in the C++ engine instead of injected JavaScript. It has not been tested by TWSC, and Canvas and WebGL spoofing need an optional bridge running on Windows.

entities/circuit-breaker-sage.md.title: Circuit Breaker Sage: reverse proxy for agent spend caps
entities/circuit-breaker-sage.md.description: Circuit Breaker Sage is a reverse proxy that catches infinite tool loops and enforces hourly and daily spend caps in RAM. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/circuit-breaker-sage.md.name: Circuit Breaker Sage
entities/circuit-breaker-sage.md.answer: Circuit Breaker Sage is a drop-in reverse proxy that stops autonomous agents from draining API budgets by catching repeated tool-call loops and enforcing hourly and daily spend caps in RAM before requests reach the upstream OpenAI API. TWSC has not tested it, and its sub-35ms overhead is an engineering target.

entities/clashmac.md.title: ClashMac: native macOS proxy client with TUN mode
entities/clashmac.md.description: ClashMac is a SwiftUI macOS proxy tool: HTTP/SOCKS5 system proxy, TUN mode, menu bar group switching, traffic topology view and rules. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/clashmac.md.name: ClashMac
entities/clashmac.md.answer: ClashMac is a native SwiftUI proxy tool for macOS with real-time traffic monitoring, topology visualization, and multi-hop transit views. It supports HTTP/SOCKS5 system proxy and TUN mode for global traffic capture, plus proxy group switching from the menu bar, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/clashmax.md.title: ClashMax: native macOS Mihomo proxy client in SwiftUI
entities/clashmax.md.description: ClashMax is a SwiftUI macOS client for Mihomo. Covers YAML profile import, proxy groups, rules, logs, system proxy and TUN modes, and the bundled core limit.
entities/clashmax.md.name: ClashMax
entities/clashmax.md.answer: ClashMax is a native macOS SwiftUI client for Mihomo that manages Clash/Mihomo YAML profiles, proxy groups, connections, rules, logs, and runtime modes, with system proxy and helper-backed TUN support. It has not been tested by TWSC, and the MVP supports only its bundled Mihomo core.

entities/claw-patrol.md.title: Claw Patrol: firewall for agent traffic, HCL rules
entities/claw-patrol.md.description: Claw Patrol is a firewall between agents and production. It reads Postgres, ClickHouse, Kubernetes and HTTP traffic and applies HCL rules.
entities/claw-patrol.md.name: Claw Patrol
entities/claw-patrol.md.answer: Claw Patrol is a security firewall that sits between agents and production environments, parsing traffic at the wire level and enforcing HCL rules with CEL expressions. It can block destructive SQL commands or pause Kubernetes operations for human approval, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/client-side-bot-detection.md.title: Client-side bot detection: signals and tamper checks
entities/client-side-bot-detection.md.description: How in-browser bot detection collects signals like mouse movement and timing, regenerates code every build, and folds tamper checks into crypto keys.
entities/client-side-bot-detection.md.name: Client-side bot detection
entities/client-side-bot-detection.md.answer: Client-side bot detection runs its checks inside the browser, the only place signals like mouse kinematics, rendering quirks, and timing jitter exist, even though the attacker controls that environment. Builds regenerate their encoding each release, and tampering corrupts a derived key instead of setting a flag. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/cloudflare-bot-management.md.title: Cloudflare Bot Management: bot detection mechanisms
entities/cloudflare-bot-management.md.description: Bot detection mechanisms: challenge checks (reCAPTCHA, hCAPTCHA, Turnstile), behavior patterning, honeypot. Not tested by TWSC yet.
entities/cloudflare-bot-management.md.name: Cloudflare Bot Management
entities/cloudflare-bot-management.md.answer: Cloudflare Bot Management is the heading of a page whose text actually describes BotScope, a platform that audits a site's anti-bot and anti-agent defenses, including challenge checks such as Turnstile, behavior patterning, network-level logging, and honeypot fake content. TWSC has not tested it, so scrapers have no reported block or bypass results here.

entities/cloudflare.md.title: Cloudflare: bot detection layers and what bypasses them
entities/cloudflare.md.description: Cloudflare's TLS fingerprinting, JSD, Turnstile and bot scoring, plus tests on Harrods and Indeed with Camoufox, Patchright, Botasaurus and unblockers.
entities/cloudflare.md.name: Cloudflare
entities/cloudflare.md.answer: Cloudflare is a CDN and network security provider whose layered bot management (TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprinting, JS detection, Turnstile, ML scoring) is configured per zone, so difficulty varies by site. In the page's tests, Harrods.com was easy (Camoufox 99%), while Indeed.com was hard (Camoufox 31%, Chrome-based tools 0%).

entities/cloudgrip.md.title: CloudGrip: self-hosted proxy to cap LLM API spend
entities/cloudgrip.md.description: CloudGrip is a self-hosted Node.js and SQLite proxy that caps LLM API budgets and stops runaway agent loops, with a dashboard for spend and token metrics.
entities/cloudgrip.md.name: CloudGrip
entities/cloudgrip.md.answer: CloudGrip is a lightweight, self-hosted AI proxy gateway and dashboard built with Node.js, Express, and SQLite that manages LLM API budgets and agent loops. It acts as a local circuit-breaker with strict budget caps and telemetry, which matters for scrapers running agents, though TWSC has not yet tested it.

entities/contabo-gmbh.md.title: Contabo GmbH: VPS host whose IPs run web crawlers
entities/contabo-gmbh.md.description: Contabo rents VPS and dedicated servers. The page covers crawler requests from its IP ranges in the Scraper Junkyard, a PHP node tree, and series B to E.
entities/contabo-gmbh.md.name: Contabo GmbH
entities/contabo-gmbh.md.answer: Contabo GmbH is a cloud provider that rents virtual private servers and dedicated servers. Web crawlers have been seen sending requests from its IP ranges into the Scraper Junkyard, a PHP-generated page tree, where the request patterns followed node numbers in series. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/coorl.md.title: coorl: curl-compatible CLI with Chrome TLS fingerprint
entities/coorl.md.description: coorl is a curl-style command-line client that sends a Chrome JA3/JA4 fingerprint. Covers how it works, its limits, and how it compares to curl-cffi.
entities/coorl.md.name: coorl
entities/coorl.md.answer: coorl is a curl-compatible command-line HTTP client by Konstantin Lebedev that sends a Chrome JA3/JA4 TLS fingerprint instead of the OpenSSL one. It only addresses TLS-layer detection, with no JavaScript execution or CAPTCHA solving, and TWSC has not tested it, so curl-cffi stays the documented choice for Python.

entities/crawl4ai.md.title: Crawl4AI: open-source crawler with LLM-ready Markdown
entities/crawl4ai.md.description: Crawl4AI is an open-source crawler that outputs Markdown for LLMs. Covers its async browser pool, caching, proxy and session control, CLI and Docker.
entities/crawl4ai.md.name: Crawl4AI
entities/crawl4ai.md.answer: Crawl4AI is an open-source web crawler and scraper that produces LLM-friendly Markdown output. It uses an asynchronous browser pool and caching, gives control over sessions, proxies, cookies, and user scripts, and runs through CLI or Docker without API keys, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/crowdsec.md.title: CrowdSec: WAF bot detection with fingerprinting and PoW
entities/crowdsec.md.description: CrowdSec is a WAF with bot detection built on fingerprinting and proof of work, plus a Kubernetes datasource using pods/logs. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/crowdsec.md.name: CrowdSec
entities/crowdsec.md.answer: CrowdSec is a Web Application Firewall with bot detection that looks at who the user is, not only what they do, and targets distributed attacks, scraping, and scalping. It combines fingerprinting with proof of work to raise the cost of botting, and it has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/curl-cffi.md.title: curl_cffi: Python TLS and HTTP/2 browser impersonation
entities/curl-cffi.md.description: Python binding for curl-impersonate that copies Chrome and Firefox TLS fingerprints. Covers a Camoufox hybrid on Akamai, HTTP/3, ETag caching and limits.
entities/curl-cffi.md.name: curl_cffi
entities/curl-cffi.md.answer: curl_cffi is a Python binding for curl-impersonate that uses BoringSSL to send Chrome or Firefox TLS handshakes. In the tests reported, it fixed httpx timeouts against Akamai on Net-a-Porter and ran about 27x faster than the browser after Camoufox handled authentication, but it cannot run JavaScript.

entities/curl.md.title: curl: HTTP request tool in the crawlerzoo catalog
entities/curl.md.description: curl entry in the crawlerzoo catalog: Kingdom Automata, Phylum HTTP, Order Crawlers, Family Search Engines. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/curl.md.name: curl
entities/curl.md.answer: curl is a bot specimen cataloged in the crawlerzoo zoo, built for making HTTP requests and listed under Kingdom Automata, Phylum HTTP, Order Crawlers, and Family Search Engines. It is identified there as a Google-Display-Ads-Bot. The source gives no technical details on how it works, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/customhouse.md.title: Customhouse: MCP proxy blocking agent data egress
entities/customhouse.md.description: Customhouse is a deterministic MCP proxy that tracks input provenance and blocks money-moving and data-egress calls after untrusted content. Includes limits.
entities/customhouse.md.name: Customhouse
entities/customhouse.md.answer: Customhouse is a deterministic MCP proxy that blocks money-moving and data-egress tool calls in AI agent sessions that have received untrusted content, based only on input provenance. Rewording or base64-ing the payload does not evade it, but the page reports a 40% false-positive rate on benign sink workflows, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/customized-firefox.md.title: Customized Firefox: patch to bypass anti-debugging
entities/customized-firefox.md.description: Firefox build that renames the debugger keyword to ticket_debugger in ReservedWords.h and CommonPropertyNames.h to bypass anti-debugging. Not yet tested.
entities/customized-firefox.md.name: Customized Firefox
entities/customized-firefox.md.answer: Customized Firefox is a modified Firefox build that renames the JavaScript `debugger` keyword to `ticket_debugger` by patching two header files in the source. This stops anti-debugging scripts on obfuscated sites from interrupting inspection, and its authors mention extending it to retrieve encryption keys from anti-bot scripts. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/d-nw.md.title: Dánwò: open-source end-to-end testing for web and mobile
entities/d-nw.md.description: Dánwò is an open-source end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile. Covers UI locators, agent steps, provider emulation, invariants and danwo matrix.
entities/d-nw.md.name: Dánwò
entities/d-nw.md.answer: Dánwò is an open-source end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps that drives the UI with locators and plain-English agent steps and checks backend effects. It emulates providers like Stripe and Slack behind a proxy, but it is a testing tool, and TWSC has not tested it for scraping.

entities/danubia.md.title: Danubia: URL to clean markdown text extraction API
entities/danubia.md.description: Danubia takes a URL and returns the main content as clean markdown. Covers its extraction library, polite crawling, shared cache and batch API.
entities/danubia.md.name: Danubia
entities/danubia.md.answer: Danubia is a text extraction API that takes a URL and returns the page's main content as clean markdown, using its own extraction library inspired by Trafilatura. For scrapers, it offers polite crawling with per-domain limits, a shared cache with cheaper cached fetches, and a batch API. It has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/datadome.md.title: DataDome: behavioral bot detection and what bypasses it
entities/datadome.md.description: How Datadome scores sessions on mouse movement, timing and fingerprint coherence, with tests on Hermes, Footlocker, Idealista and leboncoin.fr.
entities/datadome.md.name: DataDome
entities/datadome.md.answer: DataDome is a bot protection service that scores each session continuously, mainly on behavior such as request sequences, timing, and mouse movement, plus fingerprint coherence. In the reported tests, stock Chrome Playwright and default Scrapy were blocked, while Firefox, Brave, mobile impersonation, Camoufox with residential proxies, and Ghost Cursor passed on some targets.

entities/device-and-browser-info.md.title: Device and Browser Info: fingerprint test for bots
entities/device-and-browser-info.md.description: Bot detection and fingerprinting tools: a fingerprint-only bot test, your browser fingerprint, HTTP headers, and disposable email and phone lists.
entities/device-and-browser-info.md.name: Device and Browser Info
entities/device-and-browser-info.md.answer: Device and Browser Info is a platform with tools and articles on browser fingerprinting and bot detection, including a page that tests whether a bot is detected from fingerprinting signals alone. Scrapers can use it to check their browser fingerprint, user agent, and HTTP headers. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/doh-proxy.md.title: doh-proxy: Go DNS-over-HTTPS proxy, setup and limits
entities/doh-proxy.md.description: doh-proxy is a simple Go proxy that forwards TCP and UDP DNS queries over HTTP/2 to upstream DoH servers. Covers its limits, such as root for port 53.
entities/doh-proxy.md.name: doh-proxy
entities/doh-proxy.md.answer: doh-proxy is a simple DNS-over-HTTPS proxy written in Go that accepts DNS queries over TCP and UDP and forwards them to one or more upstream DoH servers using HTTP/2. It has not been tested by TWSC. Binding port 53 needs root, and a bootstrap DNS server by IP is needed if the system resolver uses it.

entities/dolphin-anty.md.title: Dolphin{anty}: anti-detect browser for multi-account work
entities/dolphin-anty.md.description: Dolphin{anty} anti-detect browser: fingerprint parameters, Scenarios builder, Profile Synchronizer, REST API and CDP automation, free 10-profile plan, limits.
entities/dolphin-anty.md.name: Dolphin{anty}
entities/dolphin-anty.md.answer: Dolphin{anty} is an anti-detect browser built for affiliate marketing and multi-account management, with per-profile fingerprint settings, team sharing, and a Scenarios recorder. It has no SDK, so scripts use the REST API and connect over CDP. It was not in the 2024 CreepJS/BrowserScan benchmark, so fingerprint quality is untested.

entities/dzt-s-captcha-harvester.md.title: dzt's captcha-harvester: storing reCAPTCHA tokens
entities/dzt-s-captcha-harvester.md.description: dzt's captcha-harvester stores the g-recaptcha-response token after a user solves a captcha, so checkout requests can reuse it. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/dzt-s-captcha-harvester.md.name: dzt's captcha-harvester
entities/dzt-s-captcha-harvester.md.answer: dzt's captcha-harvester is a captcha harvesting tool that stores the g-recaptcha-response token so it can be reused in checkout requests. A person solves the captchas once, and the saved tokens replace manual solving on each transaction. It has not yet been tested by TWSC, so no results are reported.

entities/elcapture.md.title: elcapture: Mac HTTPS debugging proxy, with HAR replay
entities/elcapture.md.description: elcapture is a native Mac HTTPS debugging proxy. Covers breakpoints, regex and JSON rewrites, HAR replay, and scripting in JavaScript, Python or Rhai.
entities/elcapture.md.name: elcapture
entities/elcapture.md.answer: elcapture is a native HTTPS debugging proxy for Mac that lets you inspect, pause, modify, and replay traffic from apps, phones, Android emulators, and iOS Simulators. It supports HTTP/2, WebSocket, gRPC, and scripting, but it is in beta, not notarized by Apple, and not yet tested by TWSC.

entities/ember-browser.md.title: ember-browser: headless Python browser for AI agents
entities/ember-browser.md.description: Open source headless browser in Python for AI agents. Scrapes a page to markdown, searches, crawls sites, lists URLs and batch scrapes. Idles near 17 MB.
entities/ember-browser.md.name: ember-browser
entities/ember-browser.md.answer: ember-browser is an open source, headless browser written in Python for AI agents, with an idle footprint of about 17 MB and no need for Docker or API keys. It handles single-page scraping to markdown, web search, site crawling, batch scraping and natural language browser control, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/envoy.md.title: Envoy: proxy removed from Reddit's feed serving path
entities/envoy.md.description: Envoy is an infrastructure component. This page covers a Reddit engineering discussion on removing Envoy from the feed serving path. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/envoy.md.name: Envoy
entities/envoy.md.answer: Envoy is an infrastructure component discussed in connection with Reddit's feed serving path, where a source describes removing it. The page reports no scraping behavior, blocking, or test results, and TWSC has not yet tested it, so it has no practical guidance for scrapers.

entities/esp32.md.title: ESP32: MQTT TCP proxy endpoint and its limits
entities/esp32.md.description: ESP32 as the hardware endpoint of an MQTT TCP proxy: it takes tunneled CONNECT traffic from a Python proxy and opens the TCP socket. Covers limits.
entities/esp32.md.name: ESP32
entities/esp32.md.answer: ESP32 is the Wi-Fi microcontroller that serves as the hardware endpoint in an MQTT TCP proxy setup, receiving commands over MQTT and opening real TCP sockets to the target server. Its limited resources cap simultaneous connections, so it is a poor fit for multiple tabs, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/f5-bot-defense.md.title: F5 Bot Defense: behavioral AI detection and testing
entities/f5-bot-defense.md.description: F5 Bot Defense (ex-Shape Security): behavioral AI detection with no visible challenge, and how it fared in the anti-detect matrix and the Nimble browser test.
entities/f5-bot-defense.md.name: F5 Bot Defense
entities/f5-bot-defense.md.answer: F5 Bot Defense is an enterprise bot mitigation product from F5 Networks, formerly Shape Security, that relies mainly on AI-based behavioral detection. In the 2023 anti-detect matrix it was one of the harder systems to pass, even for a single page load, and the Nimble browser results were not detailed.

entities/facebookexternalhit.md.title: facebookexternalhit: Facebook crawler user agent and IPs
entities/facebookexternalhit.md.description: Facebook's link preview crawler: its user agent string, AS32934 IP origin, why the user agent alone can't verify it, and traffic spikes it can cause.
entities/facebookexternalhit.md.name: facebookexternalhit
entities/facebookexternalhit.md.answer: Facebookexternalhit is the Facebook crawler that fetches the title, short description, and favicon of a site when someone shares a link on Facebook or Messenger. Its user agent is easy to spoof, so confirm the request comes from AS32934 as well; TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/farmfence.md.title: farmfence: detecting bot farm and headless traffic
entities/farmfence.md.description: Experimental 0.x TypeScript package that flags bot farm, datacenter crawler and headless probe traffic using IP, locale, geo and funnel signals.
entities/farmfence.md.name: farmfence
entities/farmfence.md.answer: farmfence is a TypeScript package that flags traffic from known bot farms, scrapers, and headless probes by combining IP, locale, geo, and funnel signals. It is experimental 0.x and not a general-purpose bot filter; its AWS ranges also cover ordinary EC2 traffic, so treat coarse matches as soft signals.

entities/feedstock.md.title: Feedstock: TypeScript crawler on Bun and Playwright
entities/feedstock.md.description: Feedstock is a TypeScript crawler on Bun and Playwright. Covers deep crawl strategies, CSS, XPath and regex extraction, browser backends and stealth mode.
entities/feedstock.md.name: Feedstock
entities/feedstock.md.answer: Feedstock is a TypeScript web crawler and scraper built on Bun and Playwright, with concurrent multi-page crawling, deep crawl strategies, several extraction methods, caching, rate limiting, and a built-in stealth mode. It runs on Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, generic CDP, or Lightpanda, but TWSC has not tested it yet, so its evasion claims are unverified.

entities/fender.md.title: fender: Docker socket proxy to replace Docker Hub registry
entities/fender.md.description: fender is a transparent Docker Unix socket proxy that registers as a Docker context and rewrites image pulls to a custom registry, with no Dockerfile changes.
entities/fender.md.name: fender
entities/fender.md.answer: fender is a transparent Docker Unix socket proxy that removes the lock-in to the implicit Docker Hub registry without changes to Dockerfiles, CI scripts, or CLI habits. It rewrites pulls such as docker.io/library/nginx:latest to a custom registry, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/fingerprinterjs.md.title: FingerprinterJS: browser fingerprinting and bot detection
entities/fingerprinterjs.md.description: FingerprinterJS v2.0 collects browser, system and network data points with 19 collectors to build a fingerprint and detect bots. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/fingerprinterjs.md.name: FingerprinterJS
entities/fingerprinterjs.md.answer: FingerprinterJS is a browser fingerprinting and bot detection tool whose v2.0 release has 19 collectors and a rebuilt architecture. It gathers system, browser, and network data points to build a fingerprint that can identify and block bots. TWSC has not tested it yet, so no bypass results exist.

entities/firehol.md.title: FireHOL: open proxy IP lists and coverage limits
entities/firehol.md.description: FireHOL aggregates IP feeds for blocking traffic. Covers the firehol_proxies list, its source datasets, and weak coverage of residential and ISP proxies.
entities/firehol.md.name: FireHOL
entities/firehol.md.answer: FireHOL is a community-driven project that aggregates IP lists for defenders, including open proxies, Tor exit nodes, and spam sources, with a daily updated firehol_proxies feed. For scrapers, it is a public list that shows very limited coverage of residential and ISP proxies compared to proprietary databases, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/fortress.md.title: Fortress: open-source stealth browser for anti-bot sites
entities/fortress.md.description: Fortress is an open-source stealth browser. Covers Cloudflare, CloudFront and PerimeterX bypass, SPA rendering to markdown, API recon, and DataDome limits.
entities/fortress.md.name: Fortress
entities/fortress.md.answer: Fortress is an open-source stealth browser that gets agents past anti-bot systems, and a single stealth fetch handles Cloudflare, CloudFront, and PerimeterX challenges. It renders SPA pages to markdown, but the open-source build does not reach DataDome or click-walls, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/fpscanner.md.title: FPScanner: self-hosted browser fingerprinting library
entities/fpscanner.md.description: FPScanner is a lightweight self-hosted fingerprinting library for bot detection, with anti-replay protection, payload encryption and optional obfuscation.
entities/fpscanner.md.name: FPScanner
entities/fpscanner.md.answer: FPScanner is a lightweight, self-hosted browser fingerprinting library that combines fingerprinting and bot detection, with anti-replay protection, payload encryption, and optional obfuscation to resist reverse-engineering. For scrapers, it shows what a site can collect from a browser. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/freesocks.md.title: FreeSocks: censorship-circumvention VPN with Xray VLESS
entities/freesocks.md.description: FreeSocks is a VPN for censored regions. Sign-in uses a 32-digit account number, no email or password, with an Xray VLESS subscription URL. Not yet tested.
entities/freesocks.md.name: FreeSocks
entities/freesocks.md.answer: FreeSocks is a VPN built for people in heavily censored regions that also works as a privacy-respecting VPN elsewhere. Users solve a human check to get a 32-digit account number with no email or password, then paste an Xray-powered VLESS subscription URL into a compatible client. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/geospoof.md.title: GeoSpoof: browser extension to match location to VPN
entities/geospoof.md.description: GeoSpoof overrides geolocation, Date, Intl.DateTimeFormat and Temporal APIs, blocks WebRTC leaks, and syncs to the VPN exit region. Not tested by TWSC.
entities/geospoof.md.name: GeoSpoof
entities/geospoof.md.answer: GeoSpoof is a browser extension and application that matches the browser's reported location to the active VPN server's IP. It overrides geolocation, timezone, and date APIs and adds WebRTC leak protection, but TWSC has not tested it, so its effect against anti-bot systems is unknown.

entities/ghost-cursor.md.title: ghost-cursor: human-like mouse paths for Playwright
entities/ghost-cursor.md.description: ghost-cursor generates Bezier mouse paths with Fitts's Law speed. Covers the Python port, the Datadome test on hermes.com, OxyMouse and its limits.
entities/ghost-cursor.md.name: ghost-cursor
entities/ghost-cursor.md.answer: ghost-cursor is a library that generates human-like mouse paths with Bezier curves and Fitts's Law speed, originally in JavaScript with a Python port, python_ghost_cursor. In TWSC tests it got Playwright past DataDome's behavioral check on hermes.com, but it had no effect on Cloudflare, which showed no mouse listeners.

entities/ghx.md.title: ghx: caching proxy for the GitHub CLI (gh)
entities/ghx.md.description: ghx is a drop-in gh replacement that runs a ghxd daemon over a Unix socket, caches responses with a TTL and coalesces concurrent identical requests.
entities/ghx.md.name: ghx
entities/ghx.md.answer: ghx is a caching proxy for the GitHub CLI that works as a drop-in replacement for `gh` and uses singleflight coalescing so repeated commands return instantly. A daemon, ghxd, serves cached responses by context-aware key and shares one result across concurrent requests. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/go-http-client.md.title: Go HTTP Client: Golang HTTP library and default user-agent
entities/go-http-client.md.description: Go HTTP client is the Golang library for HTTP(s) requests. The page covers its default go-http-client/1.1 user-agent string and links to TLS fingerprinting.
entities/go-http-client.md.name: Go HTTP Client
entities/go-http-client.md.answer: Go HTTP Client is an HTTP(s) client implemented in Golang for making requests from a Golang program. Unmodified, it sends a default user-agent such as go-http-client/1.1 that names the library version, and TWSC has not yet tested it, so no results are reported.

entities/gologin.md.title: GoLogin: anti-detect browser, Orbita and fingerprint test
entities/gologin.md.description: GoLogin is a cloud anti-detect browser built on the Orbita Chromium fork. Covers profiles, CDP automation, its 223/260 benchmark score and known limits.
entities/gologin.md.name: GoLogin
entities/gologin.md.answer: GoLogin is a cloud-based anti-detect browser, founded in 2019, that runs profiles on Orbita, its proprietary Chromium fork, and connects to Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium over CDP. It scored 223/260 in the 2024 benchmark against 226/260 for a real Mac, though behavioral signals still need separate handling.

entities/google-browser-scraper.md.title: google-browser-scraper: self-hosted Google SERP scraper
entities/google-browser-scraper.md.description: Python tool that scrapes Google results through a real browser and a sticky proxy, with an HTTP API and MCP server. Covers warm-up, retries and limits.
entities/google-browser-scraper.md.name: google-browser-scraper
