entities/google-browser-scraper.md.answer: google-browser-scraper is a self-hosted Python tool that scrapes Google search results through a real browser session on a user-provided sticky proxy, and it offers an HTTP API and an MCP server. Captchas and blocks come back as failures, the first query takes a few minutes to warm up, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/google-search-guard-vm-reversin.title: google-search-guard-vm-reversing: SearchGuard VM tools
entities/google-search-guard-vm-reversin.description: Offline Node.js tools for Google SearchGuard: a jsdom Proxy probe of browser reads, a VM deobfuscator and record recovery. None solve the challenge.
entities/google-search-guard-vm-reversin.name: google-search-guard-vm-reversing
entities/google-search-guard-vm-reversin.answer: google-search-guard-vm-reversing is an MIT-licensed GitHub repository of offline Node.js tools that analyze Google SearchGuard, the challenge served on cookieless searches: which browser data it reads, how its VM works, and what feeds the SG_SS token. It does not solve the challenge or generate tokens, and TWSC has not run it yet.

entities/google-searchguard.md.title: Google SearchGuard: how it detects bots, SG_SS cookie
entities/google-searchguard.md.description: Google SearchGuard serves a JavaScript VM challenge on google.com/search. Covers the SG_SS cookie, the signals it reads, the VM internals and build churn.
entities/google-searchguard.md.name: Google SearchGuard
entities/google-searchguard.md.answer: Google SearchGuard is the anti-bot challenge Google serves instead of search results when a client requests google.com/search without cookies. It runs an encrypted program in a JavaScript virtual machine to build the SG_SS cookie, so clients without JavaScript execution fail, and hardcoded logic breaks as builds change.

entities/goscrapy.md.title: GoScrapy: Scrapy-style web scraping framework for Go
entities/goscrapy.md.description: GoScrapy is a Go scraping framework modeled on Python's Scrapy. Covers its concurrency, retries with exponential back-off, cookies and export pipelines.
entities/goscrapy.md.name: GoScrapy
entities/goscrapy.md.answer: GoScrapy is a web scraping framework for Go that follows the architecture of Python's Scrapy, aimed at developers moving from Python to Go. It runs parallel scraping on Go's concurrency model and includes automatic retries with exponential back-off, cookie management, and export pipelines, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/greyfox-community-edition.md.title: GreyFox Community Edition: self-hosted LLM token proxy
entities/greyfox-community-edition.md.description: Self-hosted Docker proxy for LLM traffic: per-user token quotas, exact response cache, prompt injection guard, and logging. Setup steps and limits listed.
entities/greyfox-community-edition.md.name: GreyFox Community Edition
entities/greyfox-community-edition.md.answer: GreyFox Community Edition is a self-hosted AI traffic proxy and local operator console, run as a Docker box, that enforces per-user token quotas, caches exact responses for repeated non-streaming requests, and logs traffic. TWSC has not tested it yet, and it supports up to 5 active managed users.

entities/grith.md.title: Grith: OS-level security proxy for AI coding agents
entities/grith.md.description: Grith supervises AI coding agents with ptrace and seccomp-BPF, scoring syscalls against 18 filters for ALLOW, QUEUE or DENY verdicts, plus its limits.
entities/grith.md.name: Grith
entities/grith.md.answer: Grith is a security proxy that supervises AI coding agents at the operating system level, using ptrace with a seccomp-BPF pre-filter to score intercepted system calls against 18 filters. It allows, queues for human review, or denies actions, but it does not replace a VM or container for fully untrusted code.

entities/groxy.md.title: Groxy: Go library for building forward proxy servers
entities/groxy.md.description: Groxy is a small Go library for forward proxies: HTTP forwarding, CONNECT tunneling, middleware hooks, body transforms, and opt-in HTTPS MITM inspection.
entities/groxy.md.name: Groxy
entities/groxy.md.answer: Groxy is a small Go library for building forward proxy servers, with HTTP forwarding, CONNECT tunneling for HTTPS, middleware hooks, blocking, and body transforms. For scraping, HTTPS inspection is opt-in local TLS interception and needs the Groxy CA certificate trusted; otherwise encrypted bodies stay unreadable.

entities/guestlist-tools.md.title: guestlist-tools: check if AI agents can access a site
entities/guestlist-tools.md.description: Free Python library and HTTP API that grades domains green, yellow, orange or red for AI browser agent access against Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome and more.
entities/guestlist-tools.md.name: guestlist-tools
entities/guestlist-tools.md.answer: guestlist-tools is a free Python library and HTTP API that rates websites from green to red by how likely AI browser agents are to get through anti-bot systems such as Cloudflare, Akamai, and DataDome. Scrapers can check a domain's tier before spending requests, though TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/h5i.md.title: h5i: Rust headless browser for AI agents, no Chromium
entities/h5i.md.description: h5i is an open-source headless browser in Rust with no Chromium or V8. Covers Blitz and Boa, the request policy layer, @e3 snapshots and memory benchmarks.
entities/h5i.md.name: h5i
entities/h5i.md.answer: h5i is an open-source headless browser written entirely in Rust for AI agents, with no Chromium or V8, using Blitz for rendering and Boa for optional JavaScript. In benchmarks on simple, document-heavy pages it used roughly 80% less peak memory and ran cold one-shot reads about 5× faster than headless Chromium, though it will not beat Chromium at everything.

entities/hcaptcha.md.title: hCaptcha: how the image challenge detects bots
entities/hcaptcha.md.description: hCaptcha is a CAPTCHA that separates humans from bots with image puzzles. Covers response analysis and the Missing Arch challenge. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/hcaptcha.md.name: hCaptcha
entities/hcaptcha.md.answer: hCaptcha is a CAPTCHA service that separates human users from bots with visual challenges, usually image-based puzzles, and analyzes factors like response speed, accuracy, and solving method. One example is the Missing Arch challenge, which asks for the midpoint coordinates of a missing circle segment. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/hn-attention-cliff.md.title: hn-attention-cliff: Show HN half-life scraper and data
entities/hn-attention-cliff.md.description: Repository that scrapes 41,301 Show HN posts through the Algolia HN API and uses comment timing to measure how launch attention decays on Hacker News.
entities/hn-attention-cliff.md.name: hn-attention-cliff
entities/hn-attention-cliff.md.answer: hn-attention-cliff is a repository with the scraper, analysis, and data used to measure the half-life of Show HN launches on Hacker News. It pulled 41,301 posts from the Algolia HN API and used comment timing as a proxy for attention, since HN does not publish vote timestamps. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/hodor.md.title: Hodor: Rust reverse proxy with one shared password
entities/hodor.md.description: Hodor is a small Rust reverse proxy that gates a web app behind one shared password. Covers login flow, cookie signing, rate limits and WebSocket gap.
entities/hodor.md.name: Hodor
entities/hodor.md.answer: Hodor is a tiny Rust reverse proxy that gates a web application behind one shared password, with no user accounts, databases, or OAuth. It limits login attempts to 5 per 60 seconds per IP and does not proxy WebSockets (501 response); TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/hosts-tray.md.title: Hosts Tray: hosts file switcher and HTTPS proxy
entities/hosts-tray.md.description: Hosts Tray is a macOS and Windows tray tool that switches hosts files and runs an HTTPS reverse proxy on port 443 with a local CA and WebSocket support.
entities/hosts-tray.md.name: Hosts Tray
entities/hosts-tray.md.answer: Hosts Tray is a macOS and Windows tray tool that switches between hosts files and runs an automatic HTTPS reverse proxy on port 443 with a locally trusted CA. For scrapers it can help point test hostnames at local targets without browser warnings, but TWSC has not tested it, and the Windows build is unsigned.

entities/hrequests.md.title: hRequests: Python TLS client tested against anti-bots
entities/hrequests.md.description: hRequests is a Python HTTP client with TLS fingerprints and a .render() browser mode. Lab results on Akamai, Cloudflare, DataDome, PerimeterX, Kasada.
entities/hrequests.md.name: hRequests
entities/hrequests.md.answer: hRequests is a Python HTTP client from daijro that pairs browser-like TLS fingerprints with optional headless browser rendering in one session. In the November 2023 tests it passed Akamai, Cloudflare, and PerimeterX targets, but failed DataDome after the first request and Kasada with a blank screen.

entities/hysteria.md.title: Hysteria: QUIC-based censorship-resistant proxy
entities/hysteria.md.description: Hysteria proxy on a customized QUIC protocol that mimics HTTP/3. Lists its modes (SOCKS5, HTTP, TCP/UDP forwarding, TProxy, TUN) and auth and access control.
entities/hysteria.md.name: Hysteria
entities/hysteria.md.answer: Hysteria is a censorship-resistant proxy built on a customized QUIC protocol that masquerades as standard HTTP/3 traffic and is designed for lossy, unreliable networks. It offers SOCKS5, HTTP proxy, TCP/UDP forwarding, Linux TProxy and TUN modes, but TWSC has not yet tested it for scraping.

entities/icloud-hme.md.title: icloud-hme: CLI to generate iCloud Hide My Email aliases
entities/icloud-hme.md.description: CLI tool that automates iCloud Hide My Email alias creation, with SRP login, 2FA, multiple accounts, and the rate limits of about 5 per 30 minutes.
entities/icloud-hme.md.name: icloud-hme
entities/icloud-hme.md.answer: icloud-hme is a command-line tool that automates creating iCloud HideMyEmail aliases, handling SRP authentication, two-factor codes, and multiple iCloud accounts. For scrapers, it is capped by Apple's limits of about 5 aliases per 30 minutes per family member and roughly 700 per account; TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/iherb-cli.md.title: iherb-cli: Rust CLI to scrape iHerb past Cloudflare
entities/iherb-cli.md.description: Rust command-line tool that queries iHerb product data with headless Chromium. Covers the four extraction fallbacks: JSON-LD, JS globals, __NEXT_DATA__, DOM.
entities/iherb-cli.md.name: iherb-cli
entities/iherb-cli.md.answer: iherb-cli is a Rust command-line tool that queries iHerb product data through a headless Chromium browser and prints Markdown, with no API key required. iHerb uses Cloudflare anti-bot protection that blocks simple HTTP requests, so it falls back through JSON-LD, JavaScript globals, __NEXT_DATA__, and DOM scraping. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/impersonate-http.md.title: impersonate-http: Go client mimicking browser TLS and HTTP/2
entities/impersonate-http.md.description: Go http.Client built on uTLS that copies browser TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprints (JA3/JA4, Akamai) with Chrome, Firefox and Safari profiles, no headless browser.
entities/impersonate-http.md.name: impersonate-http
entities/impersonate-http.md.answer: impersonate-http is a Go http.Client built on uTLS that mimics a real browser's TLS handshake and HTTP/2 frames, with Chrome, Firefox, and Safari profiles. It aims to get past JA3/JA4 and Akamai HTTP/2 fingerprinting without a headless browser, CGo, or libcurl, though TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/impersonate-proxy.md.title: impersonate-proxy: Go MITM proxy for JA3/JA4 and HTTP/2
entities/impersonate-proxy.md.description: Local Go MITM proxy that sets JA3/JA4, HTTP/2 fingerprint, header order and User-Agent from one YAML file. Has a Chrome extension. Not yet tested.
entities/impersonate-proxy.md.name: impersonate-proxy
entities/impersonate-proxy.md.answer: impersonate-proxy is a local MITM proxy written in Go that controls TLS (JA3/JA4) and HTTP/2 fingerprints, header order, User-Agent, and source IP headers from one YAML file. Scrapers can route curl, browsers, or Playwright through it to change their fingerprint, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/intuned-agent.md.title: Intuned Agent: AI-generated Playwright scrapers and RPA
entities/intuned-agent.md.description: Intuned Agent builds, deploys and fixes Playwright code in TypeScript or Python, with stealth, captcha solving, AI browser libraries and scheduled jobs.
entities/intuned-agent.md.name: Intuned Agent
entities/intuned-agent.md.answer: Intuned Agent builds, deploys, and maintains Playwright code for scrapers, crawlers, and RPA automations from a prompt and schema, in TypeScript or Python. It includes stealth, authentication handling, and captcha solving, and it fixes code when target sites change, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/invisible-playwright.md.title: invisible_playwright: stealth Firefox patched in C++
entities/invisible-playwright.md.description: invisible_playwright is a Playwright replacement for Firefox patched at the C++ level. Covers spoofed layers: Navigator, WebGL, Canvas, fonts, WebRTC, audio.
entities/invisible-playwright.md.name: invisible_playwright
entities/invisible-playwright.md.answer: invisible_playwright is a patched Playwright replacement for Firefox that changes the browser at the C++ level, not in JavaScript, to pass advanced bot detection. It spoofs Navigator, screen, WebGL, Canvas, fonts, audio, WebRTC and timezone through preferences, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ipidea.md.title: IPIDEA: residential proxy network built on Android botnet
entities/ipidea.md.description: IPIDEA is a residential proxy network that enrolled 9 million Android devices via SDKs in free apps, turning home IPs into exit nodes. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/ipidea.md.name: IPIDEA
entities/ipidea.md.answer: IPIDEA is a residential proxy network that enrolled 9 million Android devices into a botnet by embedding third-party SDKs in free apps such as VPN utilities, casual games, and flashlight tools. Its exit nodes are real home IP addresses, but the devices are enrolled without clear owner consent, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/ipxo.md.title: IPXO: IPv4 leasing marketplace for static ISP proxies
entities/ipxo.md.description: IPXO leases IPv4 blocks that operators use for static ISP proxies via BYOP. Covers the abuse.radar.com WHOIS marker and reputation carryover.
entities/ipxo.md.name: IPXO
entities/ipxo.md.answer: IPXO is an IP address leasing marketplace where holders of large IPv4 blocks lease unused space, and static ISP proxy operators use it to get prefixes they route through BYOP deals with real ISPs. Its abuse contact in a WHOIS record flags a leased block, and leased blocks keep their bad reputation after reclamation.

entities/is-antibot.md.title: is-antibot: detect antibot and CAPTCHA challenges
entities/is-antibot.md.description: Library that spots antibot and CAPTCHA challenges from 30+ providers using HTTP status codes, headers, body markers and per-provider fingerprints.
entities/is-antibot.md.name: is-antibot
entities/is-antibot.md.answer: is-antibot is a library that detects antibot and CAPTCHA challenges from 30+ providers by checking HTTP status patterns, challenge signatures, response headers and body markers, and provider fingerprints. It checks providers in priority order and returns the first match, so scrapers can flag blocked responses. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ja3proxy.md.title: JA3Proxy: local proxy that rewrites TLS fingerprints
entities/ja3proxy.md.description: Go proxy that rewrites the TLS Client Hello to match Chrome or Firefox via uTLS, tested on Akamai at mrporter.com with httpx, plus its known limitations.
entities/ja3proxy.md.name: JA3Proxy
entities/ja3proxy.md.answer: JA3Proxy is a local Go proxy that uses uTLS to rewrite TLS Client Hello messages so any HTTP client presents a Chrome or Firefox fingerprint. In testing against Akamai on mrporter.com, paired with httpx for HTTP/2, it passed TLS checks that plain requests failed, though the Docker install was broken.

entities/jevcrawl.md.title: Jevcrawl: MCP server and CLI that crawls for AI agents
entities/jevcrawl.md.description: Jevcrawl is an MCP server and CLI that uses a small decision model to pick links and passages for an agent's question, with verbatim output and URLs.
entities/jevcrawl.md.name: Jevcrawl
entities/jevcrawl.md.answer: Jevcrawl is an MCP server and CLI tool that crawls websites for AI agents, using a small decision model to judge every link and passage so the agent's LLM reads only answer passages. It is described as 2x faster than an LLM-driven crawl and cheaper per task, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/jscrambler.md.title: Jscrambler: JavaScript obfuscation and how to reverse it
entities/jscrambler.md.description: Jscrambler obfuscates client-side JavaScript with string concealing, IIFE wrapping and decode functions. Covers deobfuscation by isolating decoders and ASTs.
entities/jscrambler.md.name: Jscrambler
entities/jscrambler.md.answer: Jscrambler is a JavaScript client-side security service that obfuscates code and blocks real-time debugging and tampering. It conceals strings, inflates code size, and wraps output in IIFEs, but the page says decode functions can be isolated and run, or ASTs used, to reverse it. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/kadoa.md.title: Kadoa: AI web scraping platform, features and limits
entities/kadoa.md.description: Kadoa is a commercial AI scraping platform that builds workflows from a URL and schema. Covers setup, proxy locations, a Yahoo Finance test and limits.
entities/kadoa.md.name: Kadoa
entities/kadoa.md.answer: Kadoa is a commercial AI-powered scraping platform that builds workflows from a URL and an output schema, with anti-bot bypass, proxies, and JavaScript rendering included. In the Yahoo Finance test it proposed an accurate schema, but only five proxy locations are supported, some sites are unsupported, and headers and cookies cannot be customized.

entities/kameleo.md.title: Kameleo: anti-detect browser with Playwright support
entities/kameleo.md.description: Kameleo anti-detect browser: Junglefox and Chroma engines, fingerprint profiles, a local CDP API for Playwright and Selenium, and CreepJS test scores.
entities/kameleo.md.name: Kameleo
entities/kameleo.md.answer: Kameleo is a Hungarian anti-detect browser that bundles two patched engines, Junglefox (Firefox) and Chroma (Chromium), and exposes a local WebSocket API that works with Selenium, Playwright, and Puppeteer. It scored 175/260 against a real Mac's 226/260 in the benchmark, but the WebRTC leak was a test setup error.

entities/kampala.md.title: Kampala: HTTP/S interception and flow automation
entities/kampala.md.description: Kampala by Zatanna intercepts HTTP/S traffic from websites and apps, maps tokens, cookies and sessions, and replays flows with the TLS fingerprint.
entities/kampala.md.name: Kampala
entities/kampala.md.answer: Kampala is a Zatanna tool that intercepts HTTP/S traffic from websites, mobile apps, and desktop apps in real time. It maps tokens, cookies, sessions, and multi-step flows, then replays them as automations with the original HTTP/TLS fingerprint preserved. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/kasada.md.title: Kasada: how it detects bots and what bypasses it
entities/kasada.md.description: Kasada anti-bot page: 429 first-request detection, x-kpsdk tokens, hardware fingerprinting, and tests on canadagoose.com and hyatt.com with Camoufox.
entities/kasada.md.name: Kasada
entities/kasada.md.answer: Kasada is an Australian anti-bot company that treats every request as a bot until proven otherwise, using a silent challenge and hardware fingerprinting. In TWSC tests on canadagoose.com, local setups often passed but datacenter VMs failed even with residential proxies, while Bright Data Scraping Browser and, by 2025, Camoufox, Patchright, and Zendriver worked.

entities/keyfence.md.title: Keyfence: local proxy that redacts secrets in LLM calls
entities/keyfence.md.description: Keyfence is a local proxy that checks requests to LLM APIs and applies block (403), redact (default) or placeholder mode to secrets. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/keyfence.md.name: Keyfence
entities/keyfence.md.answer: Keyfence is a local proxy that intercepts requests to LLM APIs before they leave the machine, so API keys and other secrets are not exposed. It runs in block, redact (the default), or placeholder mode, and TWSC has not yet tested it.

entities/kimurai.md.title: Kimurai: Ruby scraping framework with AI-made selectors
entities/kimurai.md.description: Kimurai is a Ruby scraping framework. An LLM writes XPath selectors on the first request and caches them. Covers supported LLMs, browsers and HTTP mode.
entities/kimurai.md.name: Kimurai
entities/kimurai.md.answer: Kimurai is a Ruby web scraping framework with an AI-assisted DSL. On the first request an LLM generates XPath selectors that are cached, so later requests extract without AI calls. It also runs as a traditional scraper with headless antidetect Chromium, Firefox, or plain HTTP, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/kittybrowser.md.title: KittyBrowser: terminal browser using kitty graphics
entities/kittybrowser.md.description: KittyBrowser renders headless Chrome inside a terminal pane via the kitty graphics protocol. Covers how it works, supported terminals and known limitations.
entities/kittybrowser.md.name: KittyBrowser
entities/kittybrowser.md.answer: KittyBrowser is a terminal browser that drives headless Chrome (or Chromium, Edge, Brave) and draws the pixels in a pane through the kitty graphics protocol, so it can sit beside coding agents. It has not been tested by TWSC, and it needs a kitty-capable terminal, so it fails in tmux, screen and on native Windows.

entities/konform-browser.md.title: Konform Browser: stealth Firefox ESR for scraping
entities/konform-browser.md.description: Stealth browser built on Firefox ESR for scraping and automation. Covers profile import from LibreWolf, Waterfox and Zen, and First-Party Isolation.
entities/konform-browser.md.name: Konform Browser
entities/konform-browser.md.answer: Konform Browser is a stealth browser built on Firefox ESR and designed for web scraping and automation. It can import profiles from Firefox, LibreWolf, Waterfox, Zen Browser and others, including cookies, history and passwords, and it updates privacy settings such as First-Party Isolation. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/latch.md.title: Latch: post-quantum TCP tunnel proxy server
entities/latch.md.description: Latch is a proxy server that tunnels legacy TCP traffic with mTLS, X25519 plus ML-KEM-768 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, with a Go control plane and Rust data plane.
entities/latch.md.name: Latch
entities/latch.md.answer: Latch is a lightweight infrastructure proxy server that tunnels legacy TCP traffic using mTLS and a hybrid X25519 and ML-KEM-768 post-quantum handshake, then ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption. It pairs a Go control plane with a Rust data plane, but TWSC has not tested it, so scraping results are unknown.

entities/layer3-intel.md.title: Layer3 Intel: residential proxy exit node detection
entities/layer3-intel.md.description: Layer3 Intel is a security firm behind the Residential Proxy Observatory, which flags devices acting as residential proxy exit nodes. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/layer3-intel.md.name: Layer3 Intel
entities/layer3-intel.md.answer: Layer3 Intel is a security firm that launched a Residential Proxy Observatory, a public interface to roughly a year of its data on devices acting as residential proxy exit nodes. For scrapers, it shows that residential exit IPs can be spotted and tied to illicit activity; TWSC has not tested it.

entities/libretto.md.title: Libretto: browser automation CLI for web integrations
entities/libretto.md.description: Libretto is an open-source toolkit from Saffron Health with a live browser CLI to inspect pages, capture network traffic, record actions and replay scripts.
entities/libretto.md.name: Libretto
entities/libretto.md.answer: Libretto is an open-source toolkit from Saffron Health that pairs a live browser with a token-efficient CLI to inspect pages, capture network traffic, record user actions, and replay them as automation scripts. It is meant to be used through a coding agent to build and fix integrations, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/lightpanda.md.title: Lightpanda: headless browser in Zig for AI and scraping
entities/lightpanda.md.description: Lightpanda is a headless browser written in Zig, with instant startup and claimed 11x speed and 9x lower memory than Chrome. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/lightpanda.md.name: Lightpanda
entities/lightpanda.md.answer: Lightpanda is a headless browser written from scratch in Zig for AI and automation, with no rendering overhead. Its benchmarks claim 11x faster execution and 9x less memory than Chrome, which matters for resource-heavy scraping, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/linkedinbot.md.title: LinkedInBot: link preview crawler, user-agent and IPs
entities/linkedinbot.md.description: LinkedInBot is the crawler LinkedIn uses to build link previews for shared URLs. The page gives its April 2024 user-agent string and its LinkedIn AS IPs.
entities/linkedinbot.md.name: LinkedInBot
entities/linkedinbot.md.answer: LinkedInBot is the scraper LinkedIn uses to fetch URLs shared in posts or messages, mainly to build link previews. As of April 2024 it sends the user-agent `LinkedInBot/1.0 (compatible; Mozilla/5.0; Apache-HttpClient +http://www.linkedin.com)` from LinkedIn Corporation IP addresses; TWSC has not tested it.

entities/llm-shield-proxy.md.title: LLM-Shield-Proxy: PII redaction proxy for LLM streams
entities/llm-shield-proxy.md.description: Reverse proxy that redacts PII and secrets in OpenAI-compatible LLM requests using regex, Shannon entropy and ONNX NER, with SSE rehydration.
entities/llm-shield-proxy.md.name: LLM-Shield-Proxy
entities/llm-shield-proxy.md.answer: LLM-Shield-Proxy is a stateless reverse proxy that redacts PII and secrets from OpenAI-compatible LLM API requests inside a corporate VPC, using Regex, Shannon Entropy, and ONNX NER. It is a data loss prevention tool, not a scraping tool, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/llmcap.md.title: LLMCap: hard dollar caps on LLM API calls via proxy
entities/llmcap.md.description: LLMCap stops LLM API calls at a set dollar limit. Covers the base_url change, daily, monthly and per-key caps, HTTP 429 response and self-hosting status.
entities/llmcap.md.name: LLMCap
entities/llmcap.md.answer: LLMCap is a managed proxy service that enforces hard dollar caps on LLM API calls across providers. Users point their client's base_url at proxy.llmcap.io, set daily, monthly, or per-key limits, and get an HTTP 429 once a cap is hit; TWSC has not tested it, and self-hosting is only on the roadmap.

entities/lte-modems.md.title: LTE modems: residential proxy pool on TP-Link M7000
entities/lte-modems.md.description: Nine TP-Link M7000/M7200 LTE modems on two Raspberry Pis, with GOST proxies, WireGuard access, Chromium IP rotation via pm2 and a recovery ladder.
entities/lte-modems.md.name: LTE modems
entities/lte-modems.md.answer: LTE modems are the physical source of a production residential IP proxy pool, built from nine TP-Link M7000/M7200 units on two Raspberry Pis, each with its own GOST HTTP proxy. A headless Chromium rotation engine reboots modems to get new IPs, but the pool is not fully available and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/lucidextractor.md.title: LucidExtractor: scraping and SEO analysis REST API
entities/lucidextractor.md.description: LucidExtractor is an enterprise scraping and SEO analysis platform with a REST API, stealth mode, anti-bot bypass and bulk processing. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/lucidextractor.md.name: LucidExtractor
entities/lucidextractor.md.answer: LucidExtractor is an enterprise web scraping and SEO analysis platform with a REST API for extracting page data and analyzing search rankings. It advertises stealth mode, anti-bot bypass, and bulk processing, but TWSC has not tested it, so those claims remain unverified.

entities/lumi-geo.md.title: Lumi GEO: Chrome extension for AI crawler visibility
entities/lumi-geo.md.description: Free Chrome extension that compares raw HTML with the rendered page to show what AI crawlers miss, reading robots.txt and structured data, with code fixes.
entities/lumi-geo.md.name: Lumi GEO
entities/lumi-geo.md.answer: Lumi GEO is a free Chrome extension that compares the raw HTML an AI crawler downloads with the rendered page a human sees, then scores the page and supplies code fixes. For scrapers, it shows which content loads only through JavaScript, such as product text and FAQs. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/makraexafirecrawl.md.title: MakraExaFirecrawl: memoized browser-use data extraction
entities/makraexafirecrawl.md.description: MakraExaFirecrawl is a work-in-progress browser-use tool from Makra. It memoizes layouts to cut cost to a vector query, with a browser harness and proxies.
entities/makraexafirecrawl.md.name: MakraExaFirecrawl
entities/makraexafirecrawl.md.answer: MakraExaFirecrawl is a work-in-progress continual learning harness for Browser-use, built to cut the cost and correctness problems of large-scale AI data extraction. It stores layouts in a memoization engine so repeat extractions cost a vector query, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/masterhttprelayvpn.md.title: MasterHttpRelayVPN: domain-fronted proxy via Google
entities/masterhttprelayvpn.md.description: MasterHttpRelayVPN is an HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy that tunnels traffic through Google Apps Script with domain fronting, no VPS needed. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/masterhttprelayvpn.md.name: MasterHttpRelayVPN
entities/masterhttprelayvpn.md.answer: MasterHttpRelayVPN is a domain-fronted HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy tool that tunnels traffic through Google Apps Script, so no VPS or server is needed. A network filter sees only traffic that appears to go to www.google.com, which may help scrapers get past firewalls, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/math-tanh.md.title: Math.tanh: OS fingerprinting via differing libm output
entities/math-tanh.md.description: How Math.tanh returns different bits on macOS (libsystem_m), Linux (glibc) and Windows (UCRT), and why that classifies the OS in browser fingerprinting.
entities/math-tanh.md.name: Math.tanh
entities/math-tanh.md.answer: Math.tanh is a JavaScript function whose exact output bits differ by operating system, because macOS, Linux, and Windows each use a different math library. Sites can use it as a subtle fingerprinting signal to spot a spoofed OS, and it has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/medium-good-words-solver.md.title: Medium Good Words Solver: Chrome extension for the game
entities/medium-good-words-solver.md.description: Chrome extension that solves Medium's Good Words 5x5 grid game with a trie built from words.txt, predicts solo boards by round number and submits words.
entities/medium-good-words-solver.md.name: Medium Good Words Solver
entities/medium-good-words-solver.md.answer: Medium Good Words Solver is a Chrome extension that plays the Good Words game on Medium, a multiplayer word game on a 5x5 letter grid. It loads the game's dictionary into a trie to find words of four or more letters, and it predicts solo boards from the round number. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/meshscrape.md.title: MeshScrape: peer-to-peer residential proxy network
entities/meshscrape.md.description: MeshScrape routes requests through a peer-to-peer network of real residential devices via REST API or SDK. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/meshscrape.md.name: MeshScrape
entities/meshscrape.md.answer: MeshScrape is a service that offers a distributed, peer-to-peer IP network of real residential devices for web scraping, meant to avoid blocks and rate limits. You send a target URL through a REST API or SDK and get back HTML or JSON, though TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/midnight-mimosa-malware.md.title: Midnight Mimosa malware: Android firmware proxies
entities/midnight-mimosa-malware.md.description: Midnight Mimosa is malware preinstalled in firmware of low-cost MediaTek Android phones. Covers ad fraud, silent installs, and residential proxy use.
entities/midnight-mimosa-malware.md.name: Midnight Mimosa malware
entities/midnight-mimosa-malware.md.answer: Midnight Mimosa malware is a campaign found in the firmware of low-cost Android phones with MediaTek chipsets, giving it system-level privileges to install apps silently, commit ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxies. For scrapers, it shows where some residential proxy traffic can come from. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/mitmcloak.md.title: mitmcloak: mitmproxy addon that mirrors TLS and HTTP/2
entities/mitmcloak.md.description: mitmproxy addon that reads the client's ClientHello and HTTP/2 preface and replays them upstream via an httpcloak preset. Covers QUIC and pinning limits.
entities/mitmcloak.md.name: mitmcloak
entities/mitmcloak.md.answer: mitmcloak is a drop-in mitmproxy addon that replaces the proxy's upstream leg by reading the client's real TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprints and replaying them through an httpcloak preset. It has not been tested by TWSC, and it cannot see QUIC/HTTP3 clients or clients that pin certificates.

entities/mitmproxy.md.title: mitmproxy: Python interceptor that blocks telemetry
entities/mitmproxy.md.description: mitmproxy is a Python interceptor used in the simple-proxy project. Its addon logs requests and returns 202 {"status":"ok"} for telemetry endpoints.
entities/mitmproxy.md.name: mitmproxy
entities/mitmproxy.md.answer: mitmproxy is a small Python interceptor used to build a proxy, as in the simple-proxy project. Its bundled addon logs every request and returns a 202 {"status":"ok"} response for telemetry endpoints, so applications keep working while those providers are blocked. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/mitty.md.title: Mitty: proxy RPC for method chains from Web Workers
entities/mitty.md.description: Mitty is a proxy RPC that records method chains in a Web Worker and replays them on the main thread. Lists transports and the Blob worker limitation.
entities/mitty.md.name: Mitty
entities/mitty.md.answer: Mitty is a transport-agnostic proxy RPC that runs method chains from isolated contexts such as Web Workers, browser tabs, or servers, using lazy evaluation. Real objects stay on the main thread while a proxy records calls, and TWSC has not tested it yet. Blob-created workers need an absolute URL in importScripts().

entities/mnemonic-proxy.md.title: Mnemonic Proxy: HTTP proxy for coding agent history
entities/mnemonic-proxy.md.description: Transparent proxy between a coding agent and local models. Speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Responses, and keeps history on disk.
entities/mnemonic-proxy.md.name: Mnemonic Proxy
entities/mnemonic-proxy.md.answer: Mnemonic Proxy is a transparent HTTP proxy that sits between a coding agent and local models or OpenAI-compatible servers, deciding which parts of the conversation the model reads while keeping the full history on disk. It is a tool for LLM agent workflows rather than scraping, and TWSC has not tested it.

entities/mochi-js.md.title: mochi.js: Bun CDP framework for coherent fingerprints
entities/mochi-js.md.description: Bun-native raw-CDP automation framework. Covers its 48-rule fingerprint DAG, Chromium-native fetch for JA4/JA3/H2, and humanClick and humanType.
entities/mochi-js.md.name: mochi.js
entities/mochi-js.md.answer: mochi.js is a Bun-native browser automation framework that talks to Chromium over raw CDP and derives canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, and WebGPU fingerprints from one profile and seed pair. It also routes fetches through Chromium so JA4, JA3, and H2 values match real Chrome. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/molehill.md.title: molehill: rotating HTTP CONNECT proxy on Mullvad VPN
entities/molehill.md.description: molehill turns Mullvad VPN into a rotating HTTP CONNECT proxy with sticky sessions and country routing. Covers WireGuard key setup and Docker. Not yet tested.
entities/molehill.md.name: molehill
entities/molehill.md.answer: molehill is a tool that turns the Mullvad VPN service into a rotating HTTP CONNECT proxy with sticky sessions and country-specific routing. Setup needs a WireGuard key registered on a Mullvad account, with the proxy details passed to the running Docker container; TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/momoproxy.md.title: MoMoProxy: free and paid HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS proxy lists
entities/momoproxy.md.description: MoMoProxy has free and paid proxy lists for HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS, with a free API and JSON, TXT or CSV export. Notes free proxy risks. Not yet tested.
entities/momoproxy.md.name: MoMoProxy
entities/momoproxy.md.answer: MoMoProxy is a service offering free and paid proxy lists for HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS, with a free API URL and exports in JSON, TXT, or CSV. It has not been tested by TWSC, and its free proxies carry risks such as data logging, ad injection, and stolen passwords.

entities/mozprox.md.title: mozprox: session-scoped web proxy with SSRF checks
entities/mozprox.md.description: mozprox rewrites origins through HMAC-signed tokens, blocks private IPs and DNS rebinding before connect, and wipes cookie and storage jars per session.
entities/mozprox.md.name: mozprox
entities/mozprox.md.answer: mozprox is a session-scoped, memory-safe web proxy built for private research and threat inspection. It rewrites origins through HMAC-signed tokens, checks resolved IPs for SSRF before connecting, and wipes per-session cookie and storage jars at session end, but TWSC has not tested it for scraping yet.

entities/mycel.md.title: mycel: Rust decentralized web crawler and search engine
entities/mycel.md.description: mycel is a Rust crawler, indexer and search engine. Covers robots.txt, 429 handling, WARC archiving, simhash dedup, tantivy BM25 and federated ranking.
entities/mycel.md.name: mycel
entities/mycel.md.answer: mycel is a fast, decentralized web crawler, indexer, and search engine written as a Rust binary. It follows robots.txt per RFC 9309, limits requests to one per host, and handles 429 responses, but TWSC has not tested it yet, so there are no results for scraping use.

entities/mysysinfo-api.md.title: MySysInfo API: browser and device data sites can see
entities/mysysinfo-api.md.description: MySysInfo API shows the system data a browser sends to websites: IP address, OS, browser version, screen resolution and device memory, and how sites use it.
entities/mysysinfo-api.md.name: MySysInfo API
entities/mysysinfo-api.md.answer: The MySysInfo API provides system information gathered from a user's browser and device, including IP address, operating system, browser version, screen resolution, and device memory. For scrapers, these are the same data points websites use for fraud detection, rate limiting, and rough location estimates from IP lookups.

entities/nakshguard.md.title: NakshGuard: reverse proxy that blocks AI agent loops
entities/nakshguard.md.description: NakshGuard is an on-premises reverse proxy between AI agents and LLM APIs. Covers its detection layers: rate limit, token limit, repetition, context velocity.
entities/nakshguard.md.name: NakshGuard
entities/nakshguard.md.answer: NakshGuard is an on-premises reverse proxy that sits between AI agents and LLM APIs and blocks runaway request loops before they burn API tokens. It tracks per-agent session state and applies rate limit, hard token limit, repetition, and context velocity checks, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ncro.md.title: ncro: Rust proxy that races Nix binary cache upstreams
entities/ncro.md.description: ncro is a Rust HTTP proxy between nix-daemon and substituters. It races upstreams with HEAD requests on narinfo lookups and stores routes in SQLite.
entities/ncro.md.name: ncro
entities/ncro.md.answer: ncro, short for Nix Cache Route Optimizer, is a small Rust HTTP proxy that sits between the nix-daemon and its configured substituters. It races all upstreams in parallel with HEAD requests on narinfo lookups, streams NAR bodies straight to the client, and keeps routes in SQLite; TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/nodejs-based-scraper.md.title: NodeJS-based scraper: collecting temporary phone numbers
entities/nodejs-based-scraper.md.description: A NodeJS scraper that collected 5,340 temporary phone numbers and 393,310 messages with sender data, used to analyze which sites and apps they target.
entities/nodejs-based-scraper.md.name: NodeJS-based scraper
entities/nodejs-based-scraper.md.answer: NodeJS-based scraper is a project built to collect temporary phone numbers and the messages sent to them, including message content and sender information. Its first run gathered 5,340 numbers and 393,310 messages for analysis of which sites and apps they target. The Web Scraping Wiki has not yet tested it.

entities/nodriver.md.title: Nodriver: Python Chrome automation without WebDriver
entities/nodriver.md.description: Nodriver is a Python library that drives Chrome without WebDriver. Covers CDP detection, Harrods.com tests behind Cloudflare, and datacenter limits.
entities/nodriver.md.name: Nodriver
entities/nodriver.md.answer: Nodriver is an open-source async Python library that drives Chrome without a WebDriver layer and passes CDP detection tests that catch Playwright and Selenium. In TWSC's September 2024 test, it opened Harrods.com from a local machine but was blocked from an AWS datacenter IP, because it does not forge fingerprints.

entities/novawire.md.title: NovaWire: native HTTP/HTTPS debugging proxy in Rust
entities/novawire.md.description: NovaWire is a Rust MITM proxy that intercepts, rewrites and replays HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSocket and SSE traffic, with a 32-512 MiB body store.
entities/novawire.md.name: NovaWire
entities/novawire.md.answer: NovaWire is a native debugging proxy built on a Rust MITM engine that intercepts, reads, rewrites, and replays HTTP/HTTPS traffic, including HTTP/2, WebSocket frames, and SSE events. It has not been tested by TWSC yet, and its body store is capped at 32-512 MiB, with truncation flagged when the cap is hit.

entities/nyxproxy.md.title: NyxProxy: self-hosted rotating IPv6 /64 proxy gateway
entities/nyxproxy.md.description: NyxProxy builds a self-hosted rotating proxy gateway from IPv6 /64 subnets. Covers how requests rotate across exit nodes and that TWSC has not tested it.
entities/nyxproxy.md.name: NyxProxy
entities/nyxproxy.md.answer: NyxProxy is a tool for building a self-hosted rotating proxy gateway from IPv6 /64 subnets, meant to replace metered residential proxy billing and avoid IP reputation problems. It spreads requests across the subnet pool to reduce rate limiting and blocking by WAFs, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/obscrd.md.title: obscrd: React DOM scrambling and AI crawler blocking
entities/obscrd.md.description: Open-source React tool that scrambles the DOM with CSS ordering and decoy characters, and blocks 20+ AI crawlers with robots.txt and server middleware.
entities/obscrd.md.name: obscrd
entities/obscrd.md.answer: obscrd is an open-source React content protection system that scrambles the DOM with CSS ordering and decoy characters, so scrapers and AI bots reading textContent get garbled text while users see normal pages. It also blocks 20+ AI crawlers through robots.txt and middleware. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/obscura.md.title: Obscura: Rust headless browser for scraping with CDP
entities/obscura.md.description: Obscura is a Rust headless browser with V8 and CDP, a drop-in for Puppeteer and Playwright. Compares memory, binary size and page load with headless Chrome.
entities/obscura.md.name: Obscura
entities/obscura.md.answer: Obscura is a headless browser engine written in Rust that runs JavaScript through V8 and speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Puppeteer and Playwright can drive it in place of headless Chrome. The page lists built-in anti-detection, 30 MB memory use, and an 85 ms page load, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/open-bullet-2.md.title: Open Bullet 2: credential stuffing tool for scraping
entities/open-bullet-2.md.description: Open Bullet 2 is a credential stuffing tool also used for scraping. Covers its Puppeteer and Selenium Chrome modes and the Stacker setup.
entities/open-bullet-2.md.name: OpenBullet 2
entities/open-bullet-2.md.answer: Open Bullet 2 is a credential stuffing tool that can also be used for web scraping and automation, with Puppeteer and Selenium Chrome modes that create browser instances. For scrapers, setup means setting the Chrome path in RuriLib Settings and building a configuration in the Stacker panel. It has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/otto.md.title: Otto: remote control of live Chrome tabs via WebSocket
entities/otto.md.description: Otto controls real browser tabs remotely. A Controller sends authenticated commands to a relay daemon on port 8787 and a Chrome extension node runs them.
entities/otto.md.name: Otto
entities/otto.md.answer: Otto is a secure remote browser automation platform that controls real browser tabs without a browser farm. A Controller sends authenticated commands over WebSocket to a relay daemon on port 8787, which routes them to a Chrome extension node. TWSC has not tested it yet, so its results against anti-bot systems are unknown.

entities/owl-browser.md.title: Owl Browser: self-hosted Chromium automation engine
entities/owl-browser.md.description: Owl Browser is a self-hosted automation engine built on Chromium. It has 256 isolated sessions, fingerprint spoofing, a REST API and Docker deployment.
entities/owl-browser.md.name: Owl Browser
entities/owl-browser.md.answer: Owl Browser is a self-hosted browser automation engine built on Chromium (CEF), deployable with Docker, that runs 256 isolated sessions, each with its own fingerprint, cookies, and proxy. It spoofs canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, and GPU from 100+ device profiles, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/oxylabs-unblocker.md.title: Oxylabs Web Unblocker: anti-bot bypass API and test results
entities/oxylabs-unblocker.md.description: Oxylabs Web Unblocker is a managed bypass API. See its 96/100 score, Cloudflare, Kasada and PerimeterX results, $15/GB pricing and known limitations.
entities/oxylabs-unblocker.md.name: Oxylabs Web Unblocker
entities/oxylabs-unblocker.md.answer: Oxylabs Web Unblocker is a managed anti-bot bypass API that routes requests through Oxylabs proxies, solves CAPTCHAs, and returns rendered pages. It passed Cloudflare, Kasada, and PerimeterX targets in the tests and scored 96/100 on 101 Canada Goose URLs for $0.10, though per-GB pricing makes rendering-heavy pages costly.

entities/pagesieve.md.title: PageSieve: browser extension for CSS and XPath scraping
entities/pagesieve.md.description: PageSieve is a browser extension for declarative scraping. Define field names with CSS or XPath selectors, scrape locally, and share recipes as JSON files.
entities/pagesieve.md.name: PageSieve
entities/pagesieve.md.answer: PageSieve is a browser extension for declarative web scraping that lets users name fields and extract structured data with CSS or XPath selectors. It runs entirely in the browser, and configurations save as shareable JSON recipes, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/pangolin.md.title: Pangolin: VPN-based alternative to Cloudflare Tunnels
entities/pangolin.md.description: Pangolin pairs a client-to-site VPN with an edge reverse proxy to cloak HTTPS traffic. Covers DNS hijacking, native OS clients and known limits.
entities/pangolin.md.name: Pangolin
entities/pangolin.md.answer: Pangolin is a peer-to-peer alternative to Cloudflare Tunnels that pairs a client-to-site VPN with an edge reverse proxy, so HTTPS traffic decrypts at the local network edge and stays cloaked from the public internet. TWSC has not tested it yet, and its OS-level DNS hijacking is described as the most brittle part of the codebase.

entities/perimeterx.md.title: PerimeterX (HUMAN Bot Defender): detection and bypass
entities/perimeterx.md.description: How HUMAN Bot Defender works (Sensor, Detector, Enforcer, _px3 and _pxhd cookies, press-and-hold) and what passed on NeimanMarcus, Booking and Crunchbase.
entities/perimeterx.md.name: PerimeterX (HUMAN Bot Defender)
entities/perimeterx.md.answer: PerimeterX, now sold as HUMAN Bot Defender, is an anti-bot system that scores page loads with a JavaScript sensor and cloud ML, then challenges with press-and-hold. In TWSC's 2022-2023 tests it leaned toward IP checks, and a homepage-first visit was required everywhere; in 2024 Scrapy Impersonate passed on Booking.com and NeimanMarcus.com.

entities/pg-interleave.md.title: pg-interleave: PostgreSQL proxy for race condition tests
entities/pg-interleave.md.description: pg-interleave is a PostgreSQL wire-protocol proxy that freezes statements, holds responses, kills connections after commit and injects deadlocks via HTTP.
entities/pg-interleave.md.name: pg-interleave
entities/pg-interleave.md.answer: pg-interleave is a PostgreSQL wire-protocol proxy that sits between an application and the database to pause, reorder, and fuzz queries, so concurrency tests can reproduce race conditions on demand. It is not a scraping tool and TWSC has not tested it. It is alpha, plaintext only, and its APIs may change.

entities/php-webvpn.md.title: PHP-WebVPN: PHP hosting as a stealth VPN and proxy
entities/php-webvpn.md.description: PHP-WebVPN turns shared PHP hosting into a proxy that hides traffic in HTTPS POST requests. Covers Decoy Mode, HTTP, SOCKS5 and MTProto, and chained backends.
entities/php-webvpn.md.name: PHP-WebVPN
entities/php-webvpn.md.answer: PHP-WebVPN is a serverless tool that turns ordinary PHP shared hosting into a stealth VPN and multi-protocol proxy, wrapping traffic in HTTPS POST requests to get past censorship and DPI. It supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 and MTProto, and can chain several backends, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/pingora.md.title: Pingora: Cloudflare's Rust HTTP proxy replacing NGINX
entities/pingora.md.description: Pingora is Cloudflare's in-house Rust HTTP proxy. See why it replaced NGINX, how it improves connection reuse and TTFB, and which Cloudflare services use it.
entities/pingora.md.name: Pingora
entities/pingora.md.answer: Pingora is Cloudflare's in-house HTTP proxy, written in Rust, that replaced its NGINX service and serves over a trillion requests daily. It powers CDN, Workers fetch, Tunnel, Stream, and R2 traffic, so scrapers meet it on Cloudflare-fronted sites, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/playwright.md.title: Playwright: detection signals and stealth patches
entities/playwright.md.description: Playwright for scraping: CDP Runtime.enable and webdriver leaks, Patchright and Undetected Playwright fixes, and tests on Datadome and PerimeterX.
entities/playwright.md.name: Playwright
entities/playwright.md.answer: Playwright is Microsoft's browser automation framework for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, and the base of most TWSC browser scraping. Standard Playwright fails against strict anti-bot setups, so it needs patches such as Patchright, and Datadome pages like hermes.com also required ghost-cursor for realistic mouse movement.

entities/powblock.md.title: POWBlock: proof-of-work gate against bots and scrapers
entities/powblock.md.description: POWBlock is a C proof-of-work microservice behind a reverse proxy. Covers the controller, the SHA-256 or SHA-512 challenge and the POW_TOKEN cookie.
entities/powblock.md.name: POWBlock
entities/powblock.md.answer: POWBlock is a proof-of-work microservice written in pure C with EPOLL, placed behind a reverse proxy to gate AI scrapers, bots, and DDoS traffic. Clients without a valid cookie must mine a SHA-256 or SHA-512 hash with enough leading zeros to get a POW_TOKEN. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/pqcrypta-proxy.md.title: PQCrypta Proxy: Rust reverse proxy, PQC TLS and WAF
entities/pqcrypta-proxy.md.description: Rust Layer-7 reverse proxy with hybrid post-quantum TLS, ECH, JA3/JA4 fingerprinting, GeoIP blocking, WAF and proof-of-work challenge. Not yet tested.
entities/pqcrypta-proxy.md.name: PQCrypta Proxy
entities/pqcrypta-proxy.md.answer: PQCrypta Proxy is a Rust Layer-7 reverse proxy supporting HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3/QUIC, and WebTransport, with hybrid post-quantum TLS, JA3/JA4 fingerprinting, GeoIP blocking, a WAF, and a proof-of-work challenge. Scrapers may meet these defenses on sites running it, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/productivityproxy.md.title: ProductivityProxy: local macOS proxy, graph policies
entities/productivityproxy.md.description: ProductivityProxy is a macOS menu bar app that runs a local proxy on mitmproxy. Policies are graphs of Python nodes, grouped in modes like Deep Work.
entities/productivityproxy.md.name: ProductivityProxy
entities/productivityproxy.md.answer: ProductivityProxy is a local macOS menu bar app that runs a proxy on the user's machine, with request and response policies drawn as graphs whose nodes are small Python files. It drives mitmproxy and keeps traffic local, but TWSC has not yet tested it for scraping.

entities/proof-of-human.md.title: Proof of Human: ML bot detection from behavior signals
entities/proof-of-human.md.description: Proof of Human classifies sessions as human or bot with a machine-learning model using typing, mouse, click and scroll signals. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/proof-of-human.md.name: Proof of Human
entities/proof-of-human.md.answer: Proof of Human is a detection system that classifies web sessions as human or automated using a machine-learning model. It weighs behavioral signals such as typing, mouse movement, clicks, and scrolling, plus device signals, and appears in bot detection benchmarks against AI agents and stealth browsers. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/propylea.md.title: Propylea: Rust reverse proxy with bot-blocking gateway
entities/propylea.md.description: Propylea is a Rust L7 reverse proxy and SNI TLS multiplexer. Covers its memory vacuum, phylax threat trie with stealth 404s, and AbuseIPDB reporting.
entities/propylea.md.name: Propylea
entities/propylea.md.answer: Propylea is a Rust L7 reverse proxy, multi-domain SNI TLS multiplexer, and perimeter defense gateway that holds RSS under 15 MB. Its phylax-based pipeline checks request paths against an in-memory threat trie and serves stealth 404 responses to automated crawlers. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/proxelar.md.title: Proxelar: Rust MITM proxy with Lua scripting and TUI
entities/proxelar.md.description: proxelar is a Rust MITM proxy that intercepts HTTP/HTTPS traffic, with Lua scripting, a TUI and a web GUI, in forward and reverse proxy modes. Not yet tested.
entities/proxelar.md.name: Proxelar
entities/proxelar.md.answer: Proxelar is a programmable MITM proxy written in Rust that intercepts HTTP and HTTPS traffic, with Lua scripting, a TUI, and a web interface for inspecting and changing requests. It supports forward and reverse proxy modes, but TWSC has not tested it yet, so there are no scraping results.

entities/proxium.md.title: Proxium: self-hosted HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy gateway
entities/proxium.md.description: Proxium is an open source, Docker-based HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy gateway with admin UI for accounts, ACLs, TLS, quotas and IP pools. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/proxium.md.name: Proxium
entities/proxium.md.answer: Proxium is a self-hosted, open source HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy gateway that runs via Docker and detects the protocol from the first byte received. It manages accounts, ACLs, TLS settings, quotas, and outgoing IP pools through an admin panel and API, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/proxmint-free-proxy-list.md.title: proxmint/free-proxy-list: free HTTP and SOCKS proxies
entities/proxmint-free-proxy-list.md.description: Free HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 proxy list re-tested every 30 minutes, with JSON output, uptime and latency metrics, and honeypot risks.
entities/proxmint-free-proxy-list.md.name: proxmint/free-proxy-list
entities/proxmint-free-proxy-list.md.answer: proxmint/free-proxy-list is a repository of free HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4, and SOCKS5 proxies, re-tested every 30 minutes and published as text and JSON with uptime, latency, and anonymity data. TWSC has not tested it, and the proxies are slow, short-lived, possibly honeypots, and may carry misleading "elite" ratings.

entities/proxy-benchmark.md.title: proxy-benchmark: find if proxy, browser or target fails
entities/proxy-benchmark.md.description: proxy-benchmark runs the same targets across HTTP clients, Chromium, CDP drivers, anti-detect tools and proxy paths, logging each attempt as a JSONL row.
entities/proxy-benchmark.md.name: proxy-benchmark
entities/proxy-benchmark.md.answer: proxy-benchmark is a measurement harness that runs the same targets across combinations of proxies, browser engines, and scraping targets to find out whether a failed request comes from the proxy, the browser, the host machine, or the target. Every attempt is logged as a JSONL row, though TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/proxy-botnet-malware.md.title: Proxy botnet malware: Android car head unit attack
entities/proxy-botnet-malware.md.description: Supply-chain malware on Android car head units: the TWCore update app, JarService loader, the 'zhima' reverse proxy module and click fraud by MoYu.
entities/proxy-botnet-malware.md.name: Proxy botnet malware
entities/proxy-botnet-malware.md.answer: Proxy botnet malware is a supply-chain threat on Android car head units, spread through a rogue APK pushed via the legitimate DoFun TWCore update app. Kaspersky tied it to the MoYu group; it adds devices to a proxy botnet through a 'zhima' reverse-proxy module and runs click fraud. TWSC has not tested it.

entities/proxy-scraper-cli.md.title: proxy-scraper-cli: scrape and verify free proxies
entities/proxy-scraper-cli.md.description: Python command-line tool that scrapes HTTP, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 proxies from over 700 sources, verifies them, and serves a rotating proxy and an MCP server.
entities/proxy-scraper-cli.md.name: proxy-scraper-cli
entities/proxy-scraper-cli.md.answer: proxy-scraper-cli is a Python command-line tool that scrapes free HTTP, SOCKS4, and SOCKS5 proxies from over 700 sources and verifies each one, including checks for honeypots, injected scripts, and TLS. It can merge results into one rotating proxy and has an MCP server for AI agents. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/proxy-server.md.title: Proxy Server: route browser traffic via an Android phone
entities/proxy-server.md.description: vgaj/proxy sends browser HTTP traffic through an Android phone's mobile data. Covers the proxy server, Proxy Exit app, request flow and a diagram.
entities/proxy-server.md.name: Proxy Server
entities/proxy-server.md.answer: Proxy Server is the broker component of the vgaj/proxy project, which routes browser traffic through an Android phone's mobile data connection via the Proxy Exit app. It suits geo-restricted access when you have a trusted contact with a phone, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/proxyboy.md.title: ProxyBoy: Windows HTTP/HTTPS debugging proxy with AI
entities/proxyboy.md.description: ProxyBoy is a Windows HTTP/HTTPS debugging proxy built on Electron and http-mitm-proxy, with a Copilot AI assistant. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/proxyboy.md.name: ProxyBoy
entities/proxyboy.md.answer: ProxyBoy is a Windows-native HTTP/HTTPS debugging proxy that captures, inspects, and modifies traffic, comparable to Charles Proxy or Proxyman, with an embedded AI assistant built on the GitHub Copilot SDK. It is a personal, experimental project that TWSC has not tested, and the assistant needs a Copilot subscription while the core proxy does not.

entities/puppeteer.md.title: Puppeteer: Node.js library to control Chrome
entities/puppeteer.md.description: Puppeteer is a Node.js library that controls Chrome or Chromium over the DevTools Protocol: navigation, clicks, forms, scrolling and headless runs.
entities/puppeteer.md.name: Puppeteer
entities/puppeteer.md.answer: Puppeteer is a Node.js library that controls Chrome or Chromium through the DevTools Protocol, and it runs headless by default. Scrapers use it to navigate pages, click, fill forms, scroll, and extract data, but TWSC has not yet tested it, so no results on blocking are reported.

entities/puppetflow.md.title: Puppetflow: self-hosted Puppeteer workflow automation
entities/puppetflow.md.description: Puppetflow is a self-hosted platform built on Puppeteer to build, schedule and monitor JavaScript browser workflows, with live sessions and Docker deploy.
entities/puppetflow.md.name: Puppetflow
entities/puppetflow.md.answer: Puppetflow is a self-hosted browser automation platform, powered by Puppeteer, for building, running, scheduling, and monitoring JavaScript workflows. Scrapers can watch sessions live, take over when needed, and deploy with Docker on their own infrastructure, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/purroute.md.title: Purroute: auto-detecting proxy router and gateway
entities/purroute.md.description: Purroute detects SOCKS5, SOCKS4/4a, HTTP and HTTPS-CONNECT inbound, translates protocols, chains hops, and picks exits by username tags. Not yet tested.
entities/purroute.md.name: Purroute
entities/purroute.md.answer: Purroute is a proxy server that works as an auto-detecting router or gateway. It reads the inbound protocol (SOCKS5, SOCKS4/4a, HTTP, HTTPS-CONNECT), translates it to the upstream protocol, supports multi-hop chains, and picks exits by tags in the username. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/pw-repl.md.title: pw-repl: shared Playwright browser control for agents
entities/pw-repl.md.description: pw-repl lets a user and AI agents share one Chromium session over CDP, using a pw> prompt and the pw-repl send command. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/pw-repl.md.name: pw-repl
entities/pw-repl.md.answer: pw-repl is a Playwright-powered command-line tool that lets a user and AI agents share control of one Chromium session over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. It can attach to an existing browser or start a new one, and every command shows who sent it. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/pydoll.md.title: Pydoll: async Python CDP library, Cloudflare results
entities/pydoll.md.description: Pydoll is an async Python library on Chrome DevTools Protocol with no WebDriver. Covers its Turnstile method and poor Indeed and Harrods test results.
entities/pydoll.md.name: Pydoll
entities/pydoll.md.answer: Pydoll is an async Python browser automation library that drives Chrome directly over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, with no WebDriver layer. In the 2026 Cloudflare bypass benchmark it reached 0% on Indeed and 1% on Harrods, with silent failures, Chrome CPU spikes, and documentation that does not match the API.

entities/pyscrappy.md.title: PyScrappy: Python scraper with MCP server for AI agents
entities/pyscrappy.md.description: PyScrappy is a Python library that outputs Markdown, JSON and DataFrames. Covers self-healing selectors, TLS impersonation via curl_cffi and its MCP server.
entities/pyscrappy.md.name: PyScrappy
entities/pyscrappy.md.answer: PyScrappy is a Python scraping library that turns URLs into Markdown, JSON, or DataFrames and can run as an MCP server for AI agents. It offers self-healing selectors, TLS-fingerprint impersonation through an optional curl_cffi backend, and proxy support, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/python-requests.md.title: Requests: Python HTTP library for scraping
entities/python-requests.md.description: Python HTTP library for GET and POST requests. Covers headers, cookies, sessions, proxies and user agent changes, plus related tools. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/python-requests.md.name: Requests
entities/python-requests.md.answer: Requests (python-requests/2.31.0) is a Python HTTP library for sending HTTP(S) requests such as GET and POST. It handles headers, cookies, and sessions, and lets users add proxies and change user agents to mimic other browsers or devices. The Web Scraping Wiki has not tested it yet.

entities/qtrouter.md.title: QTRouter: proxy network tied to Chinese hackers by FBI
entities/qtrouter.md.description: QTRouter, a service the FBI tied to a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group. It allegedly managed access to IoT botnets and rented VPS proxies.
entities/qtrouter.md.name: QTRouter
entities/qtrouter.md.answer: QTRouter is a tool the FBI identified as part of a proxy device network used by a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group. Its developer allegedly gave customers access to botnets of hacked IoT devices and to rented commercial proxy servers, and TWSC has not tested it, so scrapers have no results to rely on.

entities/quiet-sky-privacy-proxy.md.title: Quiet Sky Privacy Proxy: Worker that strips client IP
entities/quiet-sky-privacy-proxy.md.description: Cloudflare Worker that strips IP, cookies, user-agent and device headers before forwarding weather requests, with upstream requests built from scratch.
entities/quiet-sky-privacy-proxy.md.name: Quiet Sky Privacy Proxy
entities/quiet-sky-privacy-proxy.md.answer: Quiet Sky Privacy Proxy is a Cloudflare Worker that sits between the Quiet Sky Android app and weather providers and strips client identity, including IP, device headers, cookies, user-agent, and tokens. It forwards coordinates at the precision the client chose, so location is not hidden. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/rama.md.title: Rama: proxy configuration for network clients
entities/rama.md.description: Rama proxy support: ProxyRoute, env variables (HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY), SystemProxyLayer for system settings, SOCKS5 and HTTPS, and PAC scripts in 0.4.
entities/rama.md.name: Rama
entities/rama.md.answer: Rama is a framework for building network clients and proxies, with support for HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS5 proxies. For scraping, it lets a client take its proxy from direct routes, environment variables, or system-wide settings, and version 0.4 added PAC script support through the rama-pac crate.

entities/rayobrowse.md.title: Rayobrowse: self-hosted stealth Chromium via Docker
entities/rayobrowse.md.description: Rayobrowse is Rayobyte's closed-source stealth Chromium with C++ patches and real-device fingerprints. Covers Docker setup, CDP, benchmark score, limits.
entities/rayobrowse.md.name: Rayobrowse
entities/rayobrowse.md.answer: Rayobrowse is a closed-source stealth Chromium browser from Rayobyte, self-hosted through Docker and still in beta. It scored 100% on the TWSC composite fingerprinting test, the highest in the set, but that run was in a controlled environment, and servers without GPU pass-through still expose SwiftShader.

entities/reader.md.title: Reader: open-source scraping engine for LLMs
entities/reader.md.description: Reader is an open-source scraping engine built on Ulixee Hero. Its scrape and crawl functions return markdown, with proxy rotation and anti-bot handling.
entities/reader.md.name: Reader
entities/reader.md.answer: Reader is an open-source scraping engine for LLMs, built on the Ulixee Hero headless browser, that returns clean markdown or HTML through two primitives, scrape and crawl. It aims to handle anti-bot defenses, TLS fingerprinting, and proxy rotation, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/real-browser.md.title: Real browser: job posting liveness checks on job boards
entities/real-browser.md.description: Real browser is a tool that checks job boards to see if postings are still live, flagging expired or removed listings and ones dead across repeated checks.
entities/real-browser.md.name: Real Browser
entities/real-browser.md.answer: Real Browser is a tool that uses an actual browser to check job boards and confirm whether job postings are still live. It flags listings that are already gone or stay dead across repeated checks, but TWSC has not tested it yet, so its results against anti-bot defenses are unknown.

entities/recaptcha.md.title: reCAPTCHA: how v2 and v3 score bots and what bypasses it
entities/recaptcha.md.description: How reCAPTCHA v2 and v3 score sessions, plus bypass tests: anchor URL token tools, commercial solvers like NextCaptcha, and Camoufox, which passed v3.
entities/recaptcha.md.name: reCAPTCHA
entities/recaptcha.md.answer: reCAPTCHA is Google's CAPTCHA system, which moved from text puzzles to invisible risk scoring in v3. In the reported tests, tokens pulled by open-source HTTP tools scored low and a NextCaptcha token still drew an error, while Camoufox passed v3 on completedns.com in June 2025.

entities/relinos.md.title: Relinos: programmable browser with a REST API
entities/relinos.md.description: Relinos renders and interacts with sites through JSON requests. Covers clicks, typing, XPath extraction, pagination, result caching and a routine registry.
entities/relinos.md.name: Relinos
entities/relinos.md.answer: Relinos is a programmable browser exposed as a REST API that renders pages, runs interactions defined in a JSON request, and extracts structured data with XPath rules. It also handles pagination, result caching, and imports routines from a registry, but TWSC has not tested it yet, so its results against anti-bot systems are unknown.

entities/residential-proxy-ips.md.title: Residential proxy IPs: where they come from, limits
entities/residential-proxy-ips.md.description: Where residential proxy IPs come from (app SDKs, bandwidth-sharing apps, provider apps) and why overlapping pools mean one block can hit several providers.
entities/residential-proxy-ips.md.name: Residential proxy IPs
entities/residential-proxy-ips.md.answer: Residential proxy IPs are addresses supplied by networks of residential devices, sourced through SDKs in apps, bandwidth-sharing applications, and providers' own apps. Providers can share overlapping pools, so a target that blocks one may block others, and the same IP across providers does not prove resale. TWSC has not tested them yet.

entities/residential-proxy-networks.md.title: Residential proxy networks: how they work and the risks
entities/residential-proxy-networks.md.description: Residential proxy networks route traffic through real consumer IPs. Covers scraping and ad verification use, app consent prompts, and smart TV app risks.
entities/residential-proxy-networks.md.name: Residential proxy networks
entities/residential-proxy-networks.md.answer: Residential proxy networks route internet traffic through real consumer IP addresses, and people use them for web scraping, market research, and ad verification. TWSC has not tested them yet. The page flags security risks, since proxy-enabled TV apps share home networks with routers, printers, cameras, and computers.

entities/residential-proxy-observatory.m.title: Residential Proxy Observatory: proxy exit tracking
entities/residential-proxy-observatory.m.description: An interface that enumerates where residential proxies exit traffic, giving researchers a global view of proxy usage. Not yet tested by TWSC.
entities/residential-proxy-observatory.m.name: Residential Proxy Observatory
entities/residential-proxy-observatory.m.answer: The Residential Proxy Observatory is a research interface that gives a global view of residential proxy activity and anonymized internet activity, built on an enumeration pipeline that tracks where residential proxies exit traffic. For scrapers it shows how proxy exit infrastructure appears to researchers, but it has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/residential-proxy-services.md.title: Residential proxy services: rented IPs and botnet abuse
entities/residential-proxy-services.md.description: Residential proxy services rent out home IP addresses to mask identity or location. Covers abuse such as fraud and scraping, and how the XCPE botnet fed them.
entities/residential-proxy-services.md.name: Residential proxy services
entities/residential-proxy-services.md.answer: Residential proxy services rent out Internet addresses so customers can anonymize traffic or spoof their location. They are a major source of unwanted traffic, including account takeover, advertising fraud, and mass scraping for AI projects, and the XCPE botnet fed them through infected devices; TWSC has not tested them yet.

entities/residential-proxy.md.title: Residential proxy: how SDKs route traffic via home networks
entities/residential-proxy.md.description: How residential proxy SDKs in apps like smart TV software route traffic through home connections, the background consent model, and the local network risk.
entities/residential-proxy.md.name: Residential proxy
entities/residential-proxy.md.answer: Residential proxy is software that routes other people's internet traffic out through a user's home network, often through SDKs embedded in apps such as smart TV apps. TWSC has not tested it yet, and the page warns that weak filtering of private or local addresses could expose the home network.

entities/resurf.md.title: Resurf: deterministic testing of AI browser agents
entities/resurf.md.description: Resurf runs browser agents on synthetic sites like shop_v1, with toggles for latency, payment outcomes, server errors and session expiry, plus step logs.
entities/resurf.md.name: Resurf
entities/resurf.md.answer: Resurf is a deterministic, reproducible test environment for AI browser agents, built on synthetic websites such as the shop_v1 e-commerce site. It injects failures like network latency, payment outcomes, server errors, and session expiration per task, and records per-step trajectories. TWSC has not yet tested it.

entities/retroweb-2-0.md.title: RetroWEB 2.0: HTTP proxy for old browsers on modern sites
entities/retroweb-2-0.md.description: RetroWEB 2.0 is a forwarding proxy that fetches HTTPS pages, strips scripts and styling, and serves HTML 2.0, 3.2 or 4.01 over plain HTTP to old browsers.
entities/retroweb-2-0.md.name: RetroWEB 2.0
entities/retroweb-2-0.md.answer: RetroWEB 2.0 is a public HTTP forwarding proxy that fetches modern HTTPS pages, strips scripts and styling, rewrites links and forms, and returns simplified HTML that old browsers can read. TWSC has not tested it, so its use for scraping is unproven, and links from the first version may no longer work.

entities/reverse-socks-go.md.title: reverse-socks-go: Go reverse proxy for SOCKS5 and HTTP
entities/reverse-socks-go.md.description: Go reverse proxy cluster with one port for SOCKS5, SOCKS4/4a and HTTP(S), exit nodes behind NAT, a multi-Tor module and MTProto Fake-TLS for Telegram.
entities/reverse-socks-go.md.name: reverse-socks-go
entities/reverse-socks-go.md.answer: reverse-socks-go is a reverse proxy cluster written in Go that accepts SOCKS5, SOCKS4/4a, HTTP, and HTTPS proxy traffic on a single port, plus Telegram's MTProto Fake-TLS. Exit nodes connect back to a control server, so they can run behind NAT or CGNAT. TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/ricci-flow-ai-web-scraper.md.title: Ricci Flow AI Web Scraper: AI Chrome extension
entities/ricci-flow-ai-web-scraper.md.description: Chrome extension that uses AI to detect fields, tables and lists on a page and export to Excel, CSV or JSON. Handles pagination and infinite scroll.
entities/ricci-flow-ai-web-scraper.md.name: Ricci Flow, AI Web Scraper
entities/ricci-flow-ai-web-scraper.md.answer: Ricci Flow, AI Web Scraper is a Chrome extension that uses AI models to detect fields, tables, and lists on a page, then exports the data to Excel, CSV, or JSON. Users point and click, and it handles pagination and infinite scroll, but TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/roblox-captchav2-bypass.md.title: Roblox captchav2 bypass: PerimeterX press and hold
entities/roblox-captchav2-bypass.md.description: How the PerimeterX press and hold captcha on Roblox login and game joins is solved: PX session, proof of work, cookie redemption, and the ~100 second limit.
entities/roblox-captchav2-bypass.md.name: Roblox captchav2 bypass
entities/roblox-captchav2-bypass.md.answer: Roblox captchav2 bypass is a method, with example code, for getting past the PerimeterX (HUMAN) press and hold captcha Roblox uses for login and game joins. It needs a PX session, a proof of work solution, and a solve within about 100 seconds. TWSC has not tested it, and some accounts get Arkose or no captcha.

entities/roxy.md.title: Roxy: Go RSS proxy that merges feeds into one
entities/roxy.md.description: Roxy is a Go RSS proxy with no external dependencies that merges feeds into one, served as XML or JSON. Covers /add, /xml, /json and /refresh endpoints.
entities/roxy.md.name: Roxy
entities/roxy.md.answer: Roxy is an RSS proxy written in Go with no external dependencies that combines multiple RSS feeds into one queryable feed, handles CORS restrictions, and serves XML or JSON. For scraping, it only aggregates feeds through endpoints like /add, /xml, /json and /refresh, and TWSC has not tested it yet.

entities/runo.md.title: Runo: LLM-based typed JSON extraction from any URL
entities/runo.md.description: Runo is an open-source tool that turns a user schema into typed JSON via Gemini. Covers smart rendering, extract, batch and crawl modes, and limits.
entities/runo.md.name: Runo
entities/runo.md.answer: Runo is an open-source tool that extracts typed, flat JSON from any URL using a user-defined schema and an LLM. It tries a plain HTTP request first and falls back to a headless browser only when needed. It requires a Google Gemini API key, returns null for missing fields, and has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/rustwright.md.title: Rustwright: Playwright-style Rust CDP automation library
entities/rustwright.md.description: Rustwright is an alpha Playwright-compatible library for Python and Node.js that drives Chromium through an in-process Rust CDP engine, with no Node driver.
entities/rustwright.md.name: Rustwright
entities/rustwright.md.answer: Rustwright is an alpha browser automation library for Python and Node.js that keeps the Playwright API but drives Chromium through an in-process Rust CDP engine, with no Node driver subprocess. For scrapers, it promises faster execution, no Playwright automation fingerprints, and trusted input via real CDP events, but only a subset of the API is bridged and it is untested by TWSC.

entities/sandbox-proxy.md.title: sandbox-proxy: Go proxy that injects credentials
entities/sandbox-proxy.md.description: sandbox-proxy is a stdlib-only Go forward proxy that injects GitHub and npm tokens into sandbox traffic, with HTTPS interception and host allowlists.
entities/sandbox-proxy.md.name: sandbox-proxy
entities/sandbox-proxy.md.answer: sandbox-proxy is a stdlib-only Go forward proxy that injects real credentials, such as GitHub or npm tokens, into outbound requests so sandboxed code can use them without seeing them. It intercepts HTTPS using a generated CA, speaks HTTP/1.1 only, and has not yet been tested by TWSC.

entities/scrapegraphai.md.title: ScrapeGraphAI: LLM scraping library, tested results
entities/scrapegraphai.md.description: ScrapeGraphAI graph types and LLM options, tests on Net-A-Porter, TripAdvisor, GitHub and BBC, a 100-URL cost run, and limits like hallucinated prices.
entities/scrapegraphai.md.name: ScrapeGraphAI
